title.en: Volume 34: Zhang Mian; Zhang Zuan; Zhang Wan
title.raw: 卷三十四 列傳第二十八 張緬 弟纘 綰 Volume 34: Zhang Mian; Zhang Zuan; Zhang Wan

sentences.zh: 梁書卷第三十四 列傳第二十八

translations.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 34, Biographies 28
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang, Volume 34, Biography 28

sentences.zh: 張緬 弟纘 綰

translations.literal: Zhang Mian; his younger brothers Zhang Zuan and Zhang Wan
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mian; Zhang Zuan; Zhang Wan

sentences.zh: 起家秘書郎，出爲淮南太守，時年十八。

translations.literal: He began his career as Secretariat Gentleman and was sent out as Administrator of Huainan, at the age of eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a Secretariat Gentleman and was appointed Administrator of Huainan at the age of eighteen.

sentences.zh: 高祖疑其年少未閑吏事，乃遣主書封取郡曹文案，見其斷決允愜，甚稱賞之。

translations.literal: The Emperor doubted that he was young and not yet versed in administrative affairs, so he sent a chief clerk to collect the commandery office documents; seeing that his decisions were entirely satisfactory, he greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu suspected that at his age he might not yet know how to handle official business, so he had a chief clerk collect the commandery archives. When he saw that Mian's rulings were sound throughout, he was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 還除太子舍人、雲麾外兵參軍。

translations.literal: Upon return he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Heir Apparent and Cloud-Banner Army External Administration Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Heir Apparent and External Administration Aide in the Cloud-Banner Army.

sentences.zh: 緬少勤學，自課讀書，手不輟卷，尤明後漢及晉代衆家。

translations.literal: Mian from youth studied diligently, setting himself lessons in reading; he never put down his scrolls and was especially versed in the Later Han and the various histories of the Jin period.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Mian studied hard, assigning himself daily reading and never laying aside his books. He was especially expert in the Later Han and the various Jin-period histories.

sentences.zh: 客有執卷質緬者，隨問便對，略無遺失。

translations.literal: When a guest brought a scroll to test Mian, he answered whatever was asked on the spot, omitting nothing.
translations.idiomatic: If a visitor brought a text to quiz him, he answered every question on the spot without missing a detail.

sentences.zh: 殿中郎缺，高祖謂徐勉曰：「此曹舊用文學，且居鵷行之首，宜詳擇其人。

translations.literal: A vacancy arose among the Palace Gentlemen; the Emperor said to Xu Mian: "This office has traditionally been filled by men of letters, and it stands at the head of the flock of officials — the candidate should be chosen with care.
translations.idiomatic: When a post among the Palace Gentlemen fell vacant, the Emperor told Xu Mian, "This office has always gone to men of letters, and it leads the ranks of court officials. Choose the appointee with great care.

sentences.zh: 」勉舉緬充選。

translations.literal: " Mian recommended Zhang Mian to fill the selection.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu Mian nominated Zhang Mian for the post.

sentences.zh: 頃之，出爲武陵太守，還拜太子洗馬，中舍人。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent out as Administrator of Wuling; upon return he was appointed Groom of the Heir Apparent and Central Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was sent out as Administrator of Wuling. When he returned to the capital he was made Groom of the Heir Apparent and Central Aide.

sentences.zh: 緬母劉氏，以父沒家貧，葬禮有闕，遂終身不居正室，不隨子入官府。

translations.literal: Mian's mother, the Lady Liu — because when her husband died the family was poor and the funeral arrangements were incomplete — for the rest of her life did not occupy the principal chamber and did not accompany her son into official quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Mian's mother, Lady Liu, had lost her husband while the family was still poor, and the funeral had never been properly completed. For the rest of her life she refused the main chamber of the house and would not set foot in her son's government offices.

sentences.zh: 緬在郡所得祿俸不敢用，乃至妻子不易衣裳，及還都，並供其母賑贍親屬，雖累載所畜，一朝隨盡，緬私室常闃然如貧素者。

translations.literal: The salary Mian received in the commandery he did not dare to use; even his wife and children did not change their garments. When he returned to the capital he turned everything over to support his mother and aid his kin. Though he had accumulated resources over many years, they were gone in a single day; his private quarters remained as empty as those of a poor commoner.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery he would not touch his official salary; even his wife and children went without new clothes. Back in the capital he gave everything he had saved over the years to his mother and to needy relatives, and in a single day it was all gone. His own household stayed as bare as that of a poor scholar.

sentences.zh: 累遷北中郎諮議參軍、寧遠長史。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to North General of the Army Consulting Aide and Chief Administrator of Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to Consulting Aide to the North General of the Army and Chief Administrator of Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 出爲豫章內史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Internal Governor of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Internal Governor of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 緬爲政任恩惠，不設鈎距，吏人化其德，亦不敢欺，故老咸云「數十年未之有也」。

translations.literal: Mian in governing relied on grace and kindness and set no traps; the clerks and people were transformed by his virtue and dared not deceive him, so the old folk all said, "Nothing like this has been seen in decades."
translations.idiomatic: Mian governed through kindness rather than traps and snares. Officials and commoners alike were moved by his example and would not cheat him. The elders said they had not seen the like in decades.

sentences.zh: 大通元年，徵爲司徒左長史，以疾不拜，改爲太子中庶子，領羽林監。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong he was summoned as Left Chief Administrator of the Ministry of State, but declined on grounds of illness; he was reassigned as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, concurrently supervising the Feathered Forest Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong he was called up as Left Chief Administrator of the Ministry of State but declined because of illness. He was then made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and put in charge of the Feathered Forest Guard.

sentences.zh: 俄遷御史中丞，坐收捕人與外國使鬭，左降黃門郎，兼領先職，俄復爲真。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief; for arresting men who had fought with foreign envoys he was demoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, but retained his former post concurrently, and soon was restored to full rank.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he became Censor-in-Chief. Because his officers had arrested men who had brawled with foreign envoys, he was demoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate while keeping his former duties on an acting basis, and before long was restored to full rank.

sentences.zh: 緬居憲司，推繩無所顧望，號爲勁直。

translations.literal: When Mian held the Censorate, he pushed the law without regard for anyone and was known as stern and upright.
translations.idiomatic: As head of the Censorate, Mian enforced the law without favor and was known for his uncompromising integrity.

sentences.zh: 高祖乃遣畫工圖其形於臺省，以勵當官。

translations.literal: The Emperor then sent a court painter to depict his likeness at the Terrace Office to encourage the officials in their posts.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had a court artist paint his portrait at the central offices as an example to other officials.

sentences.zh: 中太通三年，遷侍中，未拜，卒，時年四十二。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhong Datong he was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary; before he could take office he died, at the age of forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhong Datong he was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary, but died before he could assume the post, at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 詔贈侍中，加貞威將軍，侯如故。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously appointed him Attendant-in-Ordinary and added the title General of Upright Prestige, with his marquisate unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Attendant-in-Ordinary and General of Upright Prestige, and his marquisate was left as before.

sentences.zh: 賻錢五萬，布五十匹。

translations.literal: Funeral gifts of fifty thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted fifty thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 高祖舉哀。

translations.literal: The Emperor led mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor himself led the mourning.

sentences.zh: 昭明太子亦往臨哭，與緬弟纘書曰：「賢兄學業該通，蒞事明敏，雖倚相之讀墳典，郤縠之敦《詩》《書》，惟今望古，蔑以斯過。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhaoming also came in person to mourn and wrote to Mian's younger brother Zuan: "Your worthy brother's learning was comprehensive and his conduct of affairs clear and nimble. Though Yi Xiang read the ancient classics and Xi Hou urged the Odes and Documents, measured against men past and present, none could surpass him in this.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhaoming came in person to mourn as well and wrote to Mian's younger brother Zuan: "Your noble brother's learning was encyclopedic and his handling of affairs keen and sure. Yi Xiang pored over the ancient classics and Xi Hou drilled his men in the Odes and Documents — yet compared with the men of past and present, none could match him in this respect.

sentences.zh: 自列宮朝，二紀將及，義惟僚屬，情實親友。

translations.literal: Since joining the Eastern Palace staff, nearly two decades had passed; in official relation he was a subordinate, yet in feeling he was a close friend.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he entered the Eastern Palace staff, nearly twenty years had passed. In office he was my subordinate, but in affection he was my true friend.

sentences.zh: 文筵講席，朝遊夕宴，何曾不同茲勝賞，共此言寄。

translations.literal: At literary gatherings and lecture sessions, wandering from morning lectures to evening banquets — when had they not shared these delightful pleasures and these conversations?
translations.idiomatic: At literary salons and lecture halls, from morning outings to evening feasts — when had we not shared the same pleasures and the same confidences?

sentences.zh: 如何長謝，奄然不追！

translations.literal: How could he depart forever, suddenly never to be followed?
translations.idiomatic: How can he be gone forever, suddenly beyond recall!

sentences.zh: 且年甫強仕，方申才力，摧苗落穎，彌可傷惋。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the prime of life, just when his talents were unfolding — to cut down the young shoot and drop the ear of grain — how deeply sorrowful!
translations.idiomatic: And at the very prime of life, just as his powers were coming into their own — to cut the young shoot and let the grain fall — how heartbreaking!

sentences.zh: 念天倫素睦，一旦相失，如何可言。

translations.literal: Thinking how our family ties had always been warm, to lose him in a single day — what can be said?
translations.idiomatic: Our family ties have always been close, and to lose him in a single day — words fail me.

sentences.zh: 言及增哽，巉筆無次。」

translations.literal: Speaking of it brings choking sobs; taking up the brush, words come without order."
translations.idiomatic: Even to speak of it chokes my voice; as I set brush to paper, my words fall into disorder."

sentences.zh: 緬性愛墳籍，聚書至萬餘卷。

translations.literal: By nature Mian loved ancient texts and collected books to more than ten thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Mian loved old books by nature and amassed a library of more than ten thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 抄《後漢》、《晉書》，衆家異同，爲《後漢紀》四十卷，《晉抄》三十卷。

translations.literal: He copied the Later Han and Jin histories, collating the varying accounts of various authors, and produced the Later Han Annals in forty scrolls and Jin Extracts in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He copied out the Later Han and Jin histories, reconciling the disagreements among various authors, and compiled the Later Han Annals in forty scrolls and Jin Extracts in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 又抄《江左集》，未及成。

translations.literal: He also copied the Jiangzuo Collection, but did not finish it.
translations.idiomatic: He was also working on a copy of the Jiangzuo Collection, but did not live to complete it.

sentences.zh: 文集五卷。

translations.literal: His collected writings ran to five scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His literary collection ran to five scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子傅嗣。

translations.literal: His son Fu succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu succeeded to his titles.

sentences.zh: 纘字伯緒，緬第三弟也，出後從伯弘籍。

translations.literal: Zuan, styled Bozhu, was Mian's third younger brother; he was adopted as heir by his paternal uncle Hongji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuan, styled Bozhu, was Mian's third younger brother. He was adopted as heir by his father's cousin Zhang Hongji.

sentences.zh: 弘籍，高祖舅也，梁初贈廷尉卿。

translations.literal: Hongji was the Emperor's maternal uncle; at the beginning of Liang he was posthumously granted the post of Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji was a maternal uncle of Emperor Wu and was posthumously made Minister of Justice at the founding of the Liang.

sentences.zh: 纘年十一，尚高祖第四女富陽公主，拜駙馬都尉，封利亭侯，召補國子生。

translations.literal: At eleven Zuan married the Emperor's fourth daughter, Princess Fuyang, was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards for the Emperor's Sons-in-Law, enfeoffed as Marquis of Liting, and summoned to fill a vacancy as student of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven Zuan married Emperor Wu's fourth daughter, Princess Fuyang. He was made Commandant of the Horse Guards for the Emperor's Sons-in-Law, enfeoffed as Marquis of Liting, and enrolled as a student of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 起家秘書郎，時年十七。

translations.literal: He began his career as Secretariat Gentleman, at the age of seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a Secretariat Gentleman at the age of seventeen.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺四寸，眉目疏朗，神采爽發。

translations.literal: He stood seven feet four inches in height, with clear, open features and a bright, spirited bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven feet four inches tall, with fine, open features and a bright, commanding presence.

sentences.zh: 高祖異之，嘗曰：「張壯武云『後八葉有逮吾者』，其此子乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor regarded him as extraordinary and once said: "Zhang Zhuangwu said, 'Eight generations hence there will be one who approaches me' — is this the boy?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took special notice of him and once remarked, "Zhang Zhuangwu said that eight generations later there would be someone to rival him — could this be that man?

sentences.zh: 」纘好學，兄緬有書萬餘卷，晝夜披讀，殆不輟手。

translations.literal: " Zuan loved learning; his elder brother Mian had more than ten thousand scrolls, and day and night he pored over them, scarcely laying them down.
translations.idiomatic: " Zuan was devoted to study. His elder brother Mian owned more than ten thousand books, and Zuan read through them day and night, scarcely setting them down.

sentences.zh: 秘書郎有四員，宋、齊以來，爲甲族起家之選，待次入補，其居職，例數十百日便遷任。

translations.literal: There were four Secretariat Gentlemen; since Song and Qi this had been the entry post for great clans, with appointees waiting their turn to fill vacancies; those who held the office typically transferred after several tens or hundreds of days.
translations.idiomatic: There were four posts as Secretariat Gentleman. Since the Song and Qi dynasties this office had been the usual starting point for sons of eminent families, who waited their turn to fill a vacancy and typically moved on after only a few months.

sentences.zh: 纘固求不徙，欲遍觀閣內圖籍。

translations.literal: Zuan firmly requested not to be transferred, wishing to read through all the texts and maps in the archive.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan insisted on staying in the post because he wanted to read through the entire palace library.

sentences.zh: 嘗執四部書目曰：「若讀此畢，乃可言優仕矣。

translations.literal: He once took up the catalogue of the four categories of books and said: "When I have finished reading these, then one may speak of a superior official career.
translations.idiomatic: Once, holding the catalogue of the four library divisions, he said, "Only when I have finished these may I speak of being fit for high office.

sentences.zh: 」如此數載，方遷太子舍人，轉洗馬、中舍人，並掌管記。

translations.literal: " After several years in this way he was transferred to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Heir Apparent, then to Groom and Central Aide, in each case concurrently in charge of records.
translations.idiomatic: " Only after several years of this did he move on to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Heir Apparent, then Groom of the Heir Apparent and Central Aide, in each post keeping charge of the crown prince's records.

sentences.zh: 纘與琅邪王錫齊名。

translations.literal: Zuan and Wang Xi of Langye were equally renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan and Wang Xi of Langye were spoken of as equals in reputation.

sentences.zh: 普通初，魏遣彭城人劉善明詣京師請和，求識纘。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putong, Wei sent Liu Shanming of Pengcheng to the capital to sue for peace and asked to meet Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Putong era, Northern Wei sent Liu Shanming of Pengcheng to the capital to negotiate peace and asked to be introduced to Zuan.

sentences.zh: 纘時年二十三，善明見而嗟服。

translations.literal: Zuan was then twenty-three; when Shanming met him he sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan was twenty-three at the time. When Shanming met him, he sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 累遷太尉諮議參軍，尚書吏部郎，俄爲長史兼侍中，時人以爲早達。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Grand Marshal Consulting Aide, Director of the Personnel Section of the Masters of Writing, and shortly afterward Chief Administrator concurrently Attendant-in-Ordinary; people of the time considered him precociously advanced.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to Consulting Aide to the Grand Marshal and Director of the Personnel Section of the Masters of Writing, and soon afterward became Chief Administrator with the concurrent title Attendant-in-Ordinary. His contemporaries regarded him as precociously successful.

sentences.zh: 河東裴子野曰：「張吏部在喉舌之任，已恨其晚矣。

translations.literal: Pei Ziye of Hedong said: "Director Zhang in the post of spokesman for the throne — it is already regretted that he came to it late.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ziye of Hedong remarked, "For Zhang of the Personnel Section to hold a voice at the emperor's ear is already, in my view, much too late.

sentences.zh: 」子野性曠達，自云「年出三十，不復詣人。

translations.literal: " Ziye by nature was free and broad-minded; he said of himself, "After passing thirty I no longer call on others.
translations.idiomatic: " Ziye was by nature open and unconstrained. He said of himself, "Once I passed thirty I stopped paying calls on anyone.

sentences.zh: 」初未與纘遇，便虛相推重，因爲忘年之交。

translations.literal: " Though he had not yet met Zuan, he honored him in anticipation and thus they became friends despite the difference in age.
translations.idiomatic: " He had not yet met Zuan when he began praising him in advance, and they became friends despite the gap in their ages.

sentences.zh: 大通元年，出爲寧遠華容公長史，行琅邪、彭城二郡國事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong he was sent out as Chief Administrator to the Duke of Ningyuan and Huarong, acting in the affairs of the two commandery-states of Langye and Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong he was sent out as Chief Administrator to the Duke of Ningyuan and Huarong, with authority over the commandery-states of Langye and Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 二年，仍遷華容公北中郎長史、南蘭陵太守，加貞威將軍，行府州事。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Chief Administrator to the Duke of Huarong's North General of the Army and Administrator of Nanlanling, with the added title General of Upright Prestige, acting in the affairs of the princely establishment and the province.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became Chief Administrator to the North General of the Army under the Duke of Huarong and Administrator of Nanlanling, with the added rank of General of Upright Prestige, exercising authority over the princely establishment and the province.

sentences.zh: 三年，入爲度支尚書，母憂去職。

translations.literal: In the third year he entered the capital as Minister of Revenue; upon his mother's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he returned to court as Minister of Revenue. He left office when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 服闋，出爲吳興太守。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete he was sent out as Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he was appointed Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 纘治郡，省煩苛，務清靜，民吏便之。

translations.literal: Zuan in governing the commandery reduced troublesome regulations and aimed at quiet governance; the people and officials found this convenient.
translations.idiomatic: As administrator, Zuan cut back on burdensome regulations and governed with a light hand. Officials and commoners alike found his rule easy to live under.

sentences.zh: 大同二年，徵爲吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong he was summoned as Minister of the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Datong he was recalled to serve as Minister of the Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 纘居選，其後門寒素，有一介皆見引拔，不爲貴要屈意，人士翕然稱之。

translations.literal: When Zuan held the selection office, afterward even those of humble birth from poor gates — if they had the slightest merit — were all promoted; he did not bend to the powerful, and men of letters praised him unanimously.
translations.idiomatic: In charge of appointments, Zuan promoted even men of humble birth if they showed the slightest talent, and would not defer to the powerful. Scholars and officials praised him without dissent.

sentences.zh: 五年，高祖手詔曰：「纘外氏英華，朝中領袖，司空以後，名冠范陽。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Emperor wrote in his own hand: "Zuan's maternal clan is illustrious; in court he is a leader. Since the Minister of Works, his name has stood first in Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the Emperor wrote in his own hand: "Zuan's mother's family is eminent, and in court he stands at the fore. Since the days of the Minister of Works, his name has led all of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 可尚書僕射。

translations.literal: He is fit for Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He is fit to serve as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 」初，纘與參掌何敬容意趣不協，敬容居權軸，賓客輻湊，有過詣纘者，輒距不前，曰：「吾不能對何敬容殘客。

translations.literal: " Earlier, Zuan and He Jingrong, who shared in administration, were not of one mind. Jingrong held the pivot of power and guests crowded in; if any came to call on Zuan, he would refuse to receive them, saying, "I cannot face the leftover guests of He Jingrong.
translations.idiomatic: " Zuan and He Jingrong, who shared in high policy, had never been of one mind. Jingrong held real power and his salon was always crowded. If a visitor had first called on Jingrong, Zuan would turn him away, saying, "I will not receive He Jingrong's leavings.

sentences.zh: 」及是遷，爲表曰：「自出守股肱，入尸衡尺，可以仰首伸眉，論列是非者矣。

translations.literal: " On this promotion he submitted a memorial saying: "Since going out to guard the limbs of the state and coming in to hold the measuring rod, one may raise one's head and knit one's brows and discuss right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: " On this promotion he submitted a memorial: "Since I went out to govern a province and returned to hold the scales of office, I ought at last to be able to speak my mind and judge right from wrong.

sentences.zh: 而寸衿所滯，近蔽耳目，深淺清濁，豈有能預。

translations.literal: Yet what a narrow collar blocks stays close and blinds the ears and eyes; how could one foresee what is deep or shallow, clear or turbid?
translations.idiomatic: Yet what petty constraints bind me close at hand and shut my eyes and ears — how can I tell what is deep or shallow, clear or foul?

sentences.zh: 加以矯心飾貌，酷非所閑，不喜俗人，與之共事。

translations.literal: Moreover, to feign the heart and adorn the countenance is utterly foreign to what I am versed in; I do not like vulgar men and cannot work with them.
translations.idiomatic: Add to that the art of feigning feeling and polishing one's face — that is nothing I care to practice. I do not like vulgar men and cannot work alongside them.

sentences.zh: 」此言以指敬容也。

translations.literal: " These words were aimed at Jingrong.
translations.idiomatic: " This was plainly directed at He Jingrong.

sentences.zh: 纘在職，議南郊御乘素輦，適古今之衷；

translations.literal: While Zuan held office, he proposed that for the southern suburban sacrifice the imperial carriage should be an unadorned palanquin, which suited the mean between ancient and modern;
translations.idiomatic: In office Zuan argued that for the southern suburban sacrifice the emperor should ride in an unadorned palanquin, a compromise suited to both ancient precedent and present practice;

sentences.zh: 又議印綬官備朝服，宜並著綬，時並施行。

translations.literal: he also proposed that for seals and cords, when officials were fully equipped in court dress, they should all wear the cords — and at the time both measures were put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: he also proposed that officials in full court dress should wear their seal cords visibly, and both reforms were adopted at the time.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷宣惠將軍、丹陽尹，未拜，改爲使持節、都督湘桂東寧三州諸軍事、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to General Who Proclaims Favor and Intendant of Danyang; before he could take office he was changed to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander over the military affairs of the three provinces of Xiang, Gui, and Dongning, and Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted to General Who Proclaims Favor and Intendant of Danyang. Before he could assume the post he was reassigned as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander over the military affairs of Xiang, Gui, and Dongning, and Governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 述職經途，乃作《南征賦》。

translations.literal: On the journey to take up his duties he composed the "Rhapsody on the Southern Expedition."
translations.idiomatic: On the road south to take up his post he wrote the "Rhapsody on the Southern Expedition."

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：

translations.literal: Its words run:
translations.idiomatic: It reads in part:

sentences.zh: 歲次娵訾，月惟中呂，余謁帝於承明，將述職于南楚。

translations.literal: The year stood in Juzi, the month in mid Zhonglu; I paid homage to the Emperor at Chenming and was about to take up my duties in the southern Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In the year of Juzi, in the height of the sixth month, I paid court at the Gate of Enlightened Rule and was bound for my post in the far south.

sentences.zh: 忽中川而反顧，懷舊鄉而延佇；

translations.literal: Suddenly mid-river I turned to look back, cherishing the old homeland and lingering long;
translations.idiomatic: Midstream I turned to look back, longing for home and lingering on the shore;

sentences.zh: 路漫漫以無端，情容容而莫與。

translations.literal: the road stretched endlessly without end, my feelings vague and without companion.
translations.idiomatic: the road stretched on without end, my heart adrift and without companion.

sentences.zh: 乃弭節歎曰：人之寓於宇宙也，何異夫棲蝸之爭戰，附蚋之游禽。

translations.literal: Then I reined in and sighed: man's lodging in the universe — how is it different from snails at war for a shell, or gnats clinging to a wandering bird?
translations.idiomatic: Then I checked my pace and sighed: man's dwelling in the cosmos is no different from snails battling over a shell, or gnats riding on a passing bird.

sentences.zh: 而盈虛倚伏，俯仰浮沉，矜榮華於尺影，總萬慮於寸陰。

translations.literal: Yet fullness and emptiness lean upon each other in turn; bowing and rising, sinking and floating — we prize glory on a shadow a foot long and gather ten thousand cares into a inch of shade.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rise and fall follow one another; in every bow and lift, every sink and soar, we clutch at glory measured in a hand's shadow and pack ten thousand worries into a inch of time.

sentences.zh: 彼忘機於粹日，乃聖達之明箴。

translations.literal: Those who forget scheming on a pure day — that is the bright admonition of the sage who has attained the Way.
translations.idiomatic: To forget intrigue on a clear day — that is the bright counsel of the sage who has found the Way.

sentences.zh: 妙品物於貞觀，曾何足而繫心。

translations.literal: To savor things finely in upright contemplation — how could that be worth binding the heart?
translations.idiomatic: To savor the world in clear-sighted stillness — what is that to the heart that would be free?

sentences.zh: 撫余躬之末迹，屬興王之盛世；

translations.literal: I stroke the last traces of my own person, belonging to a flourishing age of an ascending king;
translations.idiomatic: I touch the last traces of my own life, born into an age when the throne is rising;

sentences.zh: 蒙三欒之休寵，荷通家之渥惠。

translations.literal: I have received the gracious favor of three betrothals and bear the rich kindness of families joined in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: I have enjoyed the grace of three imperial betrothals and the deep kindness of families joined as one.

sentences.zh: 登石渠之三閣，典校文乎六藝。

translations.literal: I ascended the three pavilions of the Stone Canal and supervised texts among the Six Arts.
translations.idiomatic: I entered the three halls of the Stone Canal Library and collated the texts of the Six Classics.

sentences.zh: 振長纓于承華，眷儲皇之上叡。

translations.literal: I shook out my long tassel at Chenghua and was cherished by the crown prince's supreme wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: At Chenghua I shook out my long sash and won the favor of the crown prince's keen mind.

sentences.zh: 居銜觴而接席，出方舟以同濟。

translations.literal: We sat with cups in hand, sharing the mat; we went out in the same boat to cross together.
translations.idiomatic: We sat cup to cup at the same mat and put out in the same boat to cross the stream.

sentences.zh: 彼華坊與禁苑，常宵盤而晝憩。

translations.literal: In those splendid wards and forbidden gardens we often feasted by night and rested by day.
translations.idiomatic: In the splendid wards and the imperial park we often feasted by night and dozed by day.

sentences.zh: 思德音其在耳，若清塵之未逝。

translations.literal: I think his virtuous words are still in my ears, as though clear dust had not yet passed away.
translations.idiomatic: His gracious words still ring in my ears, as though the clear dust of his presence had not yet settled.

sentences.zh: 經二紀以及茲，悲明離之永翳。

translations.literal: Two decades have passed until now; I grieve that bright separation is forever shaded.
translations.idiomatic: Two decades have brought me here, and I mourn that bright presence eclipsed forever.

sentences.zh: 惟平生之褊能，實有志於棲息。

translations.literal: Only my narrow ability through life — in truth I had the wish to rest and settle.
translations.idiomatic: My talents have always been slight, and in truth I longed only to find a place to rest.

sentences.zh: 慚滅沒之千里，謝韓哀於八極。

translations.literal: Ashamed to vanish a thousand li away, I decline Han Ai's grief at the eight extremities.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed to sink into obscurity a thousand leagues off, I refuse the sorrow Han Ai would spread to the ends of the earth.

sentences.zh: 如蓑裘之代用，譬輪轅之曲直。

translations.literal: Like straw raincoats used in turn, like wheel rims bent straight or curved.
translations.idiomatic: Like straw coats passed from hand to hand, like wheel rims bent this way or that.

sentences.zh: 愧周任之清規，諒無取于陳力。

translations.literal: I am ashamed before Zhou Ren's clear rule and trust I have nothing to offer in displaying my strength.
translations.idiomatic: I fall short of Zhou Ren's clear standard and know I have no strength worth displaying.

sentences.zh: 逢濯纓之嘉運，遇井汲之明時。

translations.literal: I meet the fine fortune of washing my tassel and encounter the bright season of drawing from the well.
translations.idiomatic: I have met the good fortune of a rinsed cap-cord and the bright season of drawing water at the well.

sentences.zh: 懷君恩而未答，顧靈瑣而依遲。

translations.literal: I cherish the ruler's grace yet have not repaid it; I look back at the spirit-locks and linger.
translations.idiomatic: I hold the emperor's grace unanswered and turn back toward the palace gates, lingering still.

sentences.zh: 總端揆以居副，長庶僚而稱師。

translations.literal: I gathered the chief ministers as deputy and led the various officials, called their teacher.
translations.idiomatic: I stood second to the chief ministers and led the ranks of officials, whom men called my pupils.

sentences.zh: 猶深泉之短綆，若高墉而無基。

translations.literal: Yet like a short rope lowered into a deep spring, like a high wall without foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I was a short rope lowered into a deep well, a high wall with no foundation.

sentences.zh: 伊吾人之罪薄，豈斯滿之能持。

translations.literal: Truly my fault is slight — how could such fullness be sustained?
translations.idiomatic: My own fault is slight — how could such a full cup be held?

sentences.zh: 奉皇命以奏舉，方驅傳於衡疑。

translations.literal: I received the imperial command to present my credentials and was just then driving the relay-chariot toward Hengyi.
translations.idiomatic: I received the imperial command to report to my post and was setting out by relay carriage for the southern marches.

sentences.zh: 遵夕宿以言邁，戒晨裝而永辭。

translations.literal: Following night lodgings I spoke of departure; I warned the morning gear for a final farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Night after night I lodged on the road and spoke of going onward; at dawn I made ready my gear for a final leave-taking.

sentences.zh: 行搖搖於南逝，心眷眷而西悲。

translations.literal: My journey swayed southward in departure; my heart clung fondly westward in grief.
translations.idiomatic: My carriage swayed southward on its way, while my heart clung westward in sorrow.

sentences.zh: 爾乃橫濟牽牛，傍瞻雉庫；

translations.literal: Then I crossed horizontally at Qianniu and gazed sidelong at Zhi and Ku;
translations.idiomatic: Then I crossed by the Ox Ford and looked aside toward the Armory and the Granary;

sentences.zh: 前觀隱脈，卻視雲布。

translations.literal: Looking forward I viewed Yinmai; turning back I gazed at Yunbu.
translations.idiomatic: Before me lay Yinmai; behind me spread Yunbu.

sentences.zh: 追晉氏之啓戎，覆中州之鼎祚。

translations.literal: I traced how the Jin house first raised arms in war and overturned the tripod-fortune of the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: I traced how the Jin dynasty first took up arms and brought down the imperial fortune of the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 鞠三川於茂草，沾兩京於朝露。

translations.literal: The three rivers region lay buried in luxuriant grass; the two capitals were wet with morning dew.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Rivers country was overgrown with wild grass, and the two capitals stood damp with the dew of morning—abandoned and gone.

sentences.zh: 故黃旗紫蓋，運在震方；

translations.literal: Thus the yellow banners and purple canopies—fortune lay in the east;
translations.idiomatic: So the yellow banners and purple canopies showed that fortune had shifted to the east;

sentences.zh: 金陵之兆，允符厥祥。

translations.literal: Jinling's omen truly matched that auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: and Jinling's portent truly fulfilled that blessed promise.

sentences.zh: 及歸命之銜璧，爰獻璽於武王；

translations.literal: When the Lord Who Surrendered came with jade in his mouth, then the seal was offered to King Wu;
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Hao of Wu surrendered with the jade disc in his mouth, the imperial seal was presented to Sima Yan;

sentences.zh: 啓中興之英主，宣十世而重光。

translations.literal: An heroic ruler opened the revival and proclaimed ten generations of renewed radiance.
translations.idiomatic: a heroic ruler inaugurated the Eastern Jin revival and proclaimed ten generations of renewed glory.

sentences.zh: 觀其內招人望，外攘幹紀；

translations.literal: Within, they drew men's esteem; without, they repelled violators of law;
translations.idiomatic: Within they won the people's trust; without they drove off those who broke the law;

sentences.zh: 草創江南，締構基址。

translations.literal: They founded the south from nothing and laid the foundations of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: they founded the realm south of the Yangtze and built its foundations from the ground up.

sentences.zh: 豈徒能布其德，主晉有祀，《雲漢》作詩，《斯干》見美而已哉！

translations.literal: Was it only that they could spread their virtue, maintain Jin's sacrifices, compose poems like "Vast Milky Way" and "Dry Bank," and win such praise?
translations.idiomatic: Was it only that they spread their virtue, kept the Jin sacrifices alive, and won praise fit for the "Vast Milky Way" and "Dry Bank" odes of the Book of Songs?

sentences.zh: 乃得正朔相承，於茲四代；

translations.literal: They came to have the calendar and imperial title pass in succession—here for four dynasties;
translations.idiomatic: They held the imperial calendar in unbroken succession through four dynasties here;

sentences.zh: 多歷年所，二百餘載。

translations.literal: Over many years—more than two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: a span of more than two hundred years.

sentences.zh: 割疆埸于華戎，拯生靈於宇內；

translations.literal: They divided the borderlands between China and the barbarians and saved the people within the realm;
translations.idiomatic: They drew the frontier between the civilized lands and the barbarians and preserved the people of the realm;

sentences.zh: 不被髮而左衽，翽明德其是賚。

translations.literal: They did not wear disheveled hair and left lapels; glorious virtue was their reward.
translations.idiomatic: They never adopted barbarian dress, and glorious virtue was their true reward.

sentences.zh: 次臨滄之層巘，尋叔寶之舊埏；

translations.literal: Next I approached the layered peaks of Cang and sought Chen Shubao's old capital mound;
translations.idiomatic: Next I came to the layered heights above the blue waters and sought the old capital mound of Chen Shubao;

sentences.zh: 蘊珠玉之餘潤，昭羅綺之遺妍。

translations.literal: It still held the residual luster of pearls and jade and displayed the remnant beauty of gauze and brocade.
translations.idiomatic: It still held the lingering luster of pearls and jade and the faded splendor of silk brocades.

sentences.zh: 懷若人之遠理，豈喜慍其能遷。

translations.literal: I cherish such a man's lofty principles—how could joy or anger move him?
translations.idiomatic: I hold in mind that man's lofty principles—surely neither pleasure nor anger could ever sway him.

sentences.zh: 雖魂埋於百世，猶映澈於九泉。

translations.literal: Though his soul lies buried for a hundred generations, it still shines clear in the nine springs.
translations.idiomatic: Though his soul has lain beneath the earth for a hundred generations, it still shines clear in the depths below.

sentences.zh: 經法王之梵宇，睹因時之或躍；

translations.literal: I passed the Buddhist temple of the Dharma King and saw one who might leap according to the times;
translations.idiomatic: I passed the Buddhist temples of the Dharma King and saw one who seized the moment to rise;

sentences.zh: 從四海之宅心，故取亂而誅虐。

translations.literal: When all under heaven set their hearts upon him, he took advantage of disorder to punish the tyrannical.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm turned its heart toward him, he seized the chaos and punished the cruel.

sentences.zh: 在蒼精之將季，剪洪柯以銷落；

translations.literal: When the green essence was nearing its end, great branches were cut to wither and fall;
translations.idiomatic: As the Chen dynasty neared its end, great branches were lopped off to wither and die;

sentences.zh: 旣觀蠍而逞刑，又施獸而爲謔。

translations.literal: They both watched scorpions and indulged in cruel punishments, and used beasts for mockery and sport.
translations.idiomatic: They built pavilions to watch scorpions and inflicted cruel punishments, and set beasts to perform for their amusement.

sentences.zh: 候高熢以巧笑，俟長星而歡噱。

translations.literal: They waited for beacon fires with crafty smiles and awaited the long comet with merry laughter.
translations.idiomatic: They greeted beacon fires with crafty smiles and greeted the long comet with merry laughter.

sentences.zh: 何惵惵之黔首，思假命其無託。

translations.literal: Why did the trembling common people find no one to whom they could entrust their borrowed lives?
translations.idiomatic: Why did the trembling common people have no one to whom they could entrust their very lives?

sentences.zh: 信人欲而天從，爰物睹而聖作。

translations.literal: Truly human desire and heaven complied; thus things were seen and a sage arose.
translations.idiomatic: Truly heaven answered human longing; the age called forth a sage.

sentences.zh: 我皇帝膺籙受圖，聰明神武，乘釁而運，席捲三楚。

translations.literal: Our Emperor received the register and accepted the chart—clear, bright, divinely martial; riding opportunity to rise, he swept through the Three Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Our Emperor received the mandate and accepted the heavenly chart—clear-sighted, divinely martial; seizing the moment, he swept through the Three Chu regions.

sentences.zh: 師克在和，仁義必取；

translations.literal: Armies prevail through harmony; victory must be taken through benevolence and righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: His armies triumphed through harmony, and he conquered through benevolence and righteousness;

sentences.zh: 形猶積決，應若飆舉。

translations.literal: His form was like an accumulated burst; his response like a whirlwind rising.
translations.idiomatic: he moved like a dam breaking, and answered like a whirlwind rising.

sentences.zh: 於是殪桑林之封豨，繳青丘之大風，戢干戈以耀德，肆《時夏》而成功。

translations.literal: Thus he killed the Fengxi of Mulberry Grove, shot down the Great Wind of Qingqiu, put away weapons to display virtue, and spread forth "Seasonal Xia" in success.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he subdued rebels as the ancient sage kings had done, sheathed the weapons of war to display his virtue, and spread the "Seasonal Xia" ode in triumph.

sentences.zh: 放流聲于鄭、衛，屏豔質於傾宮；

translations.literal: He cast out the licentious music of Zheng and Wei and banished beautiful women from the Qin Palace;
translations.idiomatic: He banished the licentious music of Zheng and Wei and drove wanton beauty from the palace;

sentences.zh: 配軒皇以邁跡，豈商、周之比靈斯。

translations.literal: He matched the Yellow Emperor in transcendent track—how could Shang and Zhou compare in spiritual power?
translations.idiomatic: He matched the Yellow Emperor in lofty achievement—how could the Shang and Zhou even be compared in sacred power?

sentences.zh: 化致長平，于茲四紀；

translations.literal: His transforming power reached long peace—for four epochs now.
translations.idiomatic: His transforming rule has brought lasting peace for four decades now;

sentences.zh: 六夷膜拜，八蠻同軌。

translations.literal: The six barbarian tribes bow in worship; the eight southern savages share the same track.
translations.idiomatic: the six barbarian peoples bow in homage, and the eight southern tribes follow the same law.

sentences.zh: 教穆於上庠，冤申於大理；

translations.literal: Teachings are honored at the Imperial Academy; wrongs are redressed at the Court of Justice;
translations.idiomatic: Learning flourishes at the Imperial Academy, and wrongs are redressed at the Court of Justice;

sentences.zh: 顯三光之照燭，降五靈之休祉。

translations.literal: He manifests the illumination of the three luminaries and sends down the blessed favor of the five numina.
translations.idiomatic: the sun, moon, and stars shine forth in his age, and the five numina send down their blessings.

sentences.zh: 諒殊功於百王，固無得而稱矣。

translations.literal: Surely his exceptional merit among the hundred kings is truly beyond what can be named.
translations.idiomatic: Surely his surpassing merit among all the kings of old is beyond what words can express.

sentences.zh: 溯金牛之迅渚，睹靈山之雄壯，實江南之丘墟，平雲霄而竦狀。

translations.literal: I went upstream to Golden Ox's swift ford and beheld Spirit Mountain's heroic majesty—truly a ruin mound of Jiangnan, level with the clouds in towering form.
translations.idiomatic: I went upstream to the swift ford of Golden Ox and beheld the heroic majesty of Spirit Mountain—a great mound of Jiangnan rising level with the clouds in towering splendor.

sentences.zh: 標素嶺乎青壁，葺赬文於翠嶂；

translations.literal: White peaks are marked on green cliffs; crimson patterns are roofed upon emerald crags;
translations.idiomatic: White peaks stand marked upon green cliffs, and crimson patterns crown emerald crags;

sentences.zh: 跳巨石以驚湍，批沖岩而駭浪。

translations.literal: Great stones leap amid startling rapids; mid-stream cliffs are struck by terrifying waves.
translations.idiomatic: great boulders leap in the startling rapids, and midstream cliffs are battered by terrifying waves.

sentences.zh: 鏟千尋之峭岸，潨萬流之大壑；

translations.literal: A thousand-fathom sheer bank is scooped out; ten thousand streams pour into a great chasm;
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-fathom cliffs are carved away, and ten thousand streams pour into a vast gorge;

sentences.zh: 隱日月以蔽虧，摶風煙而回薄。

translations.literal: Sun and moon are hidden in partial eclipse; wind and mist whirl in circling gusts.
translations.idiomatic: sun and moon are hidden in shadow, and wind and mist whirl in circling gusts.

sentences.zh: 崖映川而晃朗，水騰光而倏爍；

translations.literal: Cliffs mirror rivers in bright clarity; waters rise with light in sudden flash;
translations.idiomatic: Cliffs mirror the rivers in bright clarity, and the waters flash with sudden light;

sentences.zh: 積霜霰之往還，鼓波濤之前卻。

translations.literal: Frost and hail accumulate in alternating flow; waves beat forward and back.
translations.idiomatic: frost and hail gather and scatter, and the waves surge forward and fall back.

sentences.zh: 下流沫以洊險，上岑崟而將落；

translations.literal: Below, foam flows in repeated peril; above, peaks tower as if about to fall;
translations.idiomatic: Below, foam churns through repeated peril; above, jagged peaks loom as if about to collapse;

sentences.zh: 聞知命之是虞，故違風而靡託。

translations.literal: Hearing that fate must be feared, I therefore shunned contrary winds with nowhere to entrust myself.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that fate must be feared, I shunned the contrary winds and found nowhere to put my trust.

sentences.zh: 訊會骸之詭狀，雲怒特之來奔。

translations.literal: I inquired about the grotesque form at Huihai; clouds said Nutai came rushing.
translations.idiomatic: I asked about the strange shape at Meeting Skeleton, and was told that the raging Nutai bull came charging down.

sentences.zh: 及漁人之垂餌，沉潛鎖于洪源。

translations.literal: When the fisherman cast his bait, the hidden dragon was locked in the deep source.
translations.idiomatic: When the fisherman cast his line, the hidden dragon lay locked in the deep source.

sentences.zh: 鑒幽塗于忠武，馳四馬之高軒。

translations.literal: I took the hidden path as my mirror at Loyal Martial and drove a four-horse carriage on a high chariot.
translations.idiomatic: I took instruction from the hidden path at Zhuge Liang's shrine and drove my four-horse carriage along the high road.

sentences.zh: 不語神以征怪，情存之而勿論。

translations.literal: I did not speak of spirits to vindicate marvels; the feeling remained but I did not discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: I did not invoke spirits to prove wonders; the feeling stayed with me, but I kept it unspoken.

sentences.zh: 曬姑孰之舊朔，訪遺迹兮宣武；

translations.literal: Sunlight fell on Gushu's old north wall; I visited traces at Xuanwu;
translations.idiomatic: Sunlight fell on the old north wall of Gushu, and I visited the traces at Xuanwu;

sentences.zh: 挾仲謀之雄氣，朝委裘而作輔。

translations.literal: Bearing Sun Quan's heroic spirit, at court he wore fur and served as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan carried heroic spirit within him; at court he wore fur robes and served as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 歷祖宗之明君，猶負芒於盛主；

translations.literal: Through generations of enlightened rulers, they still stood in awe before this powerful lord;
translations.idiomatic: Through generations of enlightened rulers, his ministers still stood in awe before so mighty a lord;

sentences.zh: 勢傾河以覆岱，威回天而震宇。

translations.literal: His power could tilt the river to cover Mount Dai; his authority could turn heaven and shake the realm.
translations.idiomatic: His power could tilt the Yellow River to cover Mount Tai; his authority could turn heaven itself and shake the world.

sentences.zh: 雖明允之篤誠，在伊、稷而未舉；

translations.literal: Though in devoted sincerity like Mingyun, like Yi Yin and Hou Ji he had not yet been fully raised to employ;
translations.idiomatic: Though ministers as sincere as Zhuge Liang stood ready, like Yi Yin and Hou Ji they were not yet fully employed;

sentences.zh: 矧有功而無志，豈季葉其能處。

translations.literal: How much less one with merit but no resolve—could the declining age sustain him?
translations.idiomatic: How much less could those who had power but no resolve hold the realm in its declining years?

sentences.zh: 懼貽笑於文、景，憂象賢之覆餗；

translations.literal: They feared becoming a laughingstock like Emperors Wen and Jing and worried that "the elephant breeds virtue" would ruin the meal.
translations.idiomatic: They feared becoming laughingstocks like the Wen and Jing emperors and dreaded that a virtuous heir might still ruin everything at the last.

sentences.zh: 雖苞蘖以代興，終夷宗而殄族。

translations.literal: Though shoots replaced the withered trunk, in the end the clan was exterminated and the house destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Though new shoots rose from the withered trunk, in the end the house was exterminated root and branch.

sentences.zh: 彼儋石之贏儲，尚邀之而俟福；

translations.literal: Those with merely a stone's measure of stored grain still hoped for and awaited fortune;
translations.idiomatic: Men who hoarded no more than a few bushels of grain still prayed and waited for fortune;

sentences.zh: 況神明之大寶，乃闇干於天祿。

translations.literal: How much more the great treasure of the divine mandate—yet it was obscured from heaven's stipend.
translations.idiomatic: how much more the great treasure of the throne—yet it was cut off from heaven's favor.

sentences.zh: 造扃鍵之候司，發傳書于關尉；

translations.literal: I made bolts and keys for the gate officials and issued transit passes to the frontier guards;
translations.idiomatic: The gate officials set bolts and keys, and the frontier guards issued transit passes;

sentences.zh: 據蒐轅乎伊洛，守衡津於河渭。

translations.literal: They held the strategic hub at Yiluo and guarded the ford at He and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: They held the strategic crossroads of Yiluo and guarded the fords of the He and Wei rivers.

sentences.zh: 無矯且以招賓，闕捐繻而待貴。

translations.literal: Without false display to attract guests, lacking the gift of a silk token for awaiting nobility.
translations.idiomatic: There was no pretense to lure travelers in, nor any need to surrender a silk passport to await the great.

sentences.zh: 賓祗敬於王典，懷鞠躬而屏氣。

translations.literal: The guest reverently observed court ritual, bowing deeply and holding his breath.
translations.idiomatic: The traveler reverently observed court ritual, bowing deeply and holding his breath.

sentences.zh: 惟函谷之襟帶，疑武庫之精兵。

translations.literal: Only Hangu Pass as strategic belt— as if an arsenal of elite troops.
translations.idiomatic: Only Hangu Pass, girdling the land like a belt, seemed an arsenal stocked with elite troops.

sentences.zh: 采風謠於往昔，聞乳虎於寧成。

translations.literal: I gathered folk songs of past days and heard of the tiger cub at Ning Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: I gathered the folk songs of old and heard tell of Ning Cheng and his tiger cub.

sentences.zh: 在當今而簡易，止譏鑒其姦情；

translations.literal: In the present day it is simplified—only inspect and expose criminal hearts;
translations.idiomatic: In our own day the passage is easy, and the guards need only inspect and expose wrongdoing;

sentences.zh: 陋文仲之廢職，鄙耏門之食征。

translations.literal: I despise Wen Zhong's neglect of duty and scorn Ermen's food tax.
translations.idiomatic: I scorn Wen Zhong for neglecting his post and despise Ermen for levying taxes on cattle feed.

sentences.zh: 於是近睇赭岑，遙瞻鵲岸，島嶼蒼茫，風雲蕭散。

translations.literal: Then I looked close at Zhucen and gazed afar at Quebank—islands hazy, wind and clouds scattered thin.
translations.idiomatic: Then I looked close at Red Peak and gazed far toward Magpie Bank—islands blurred in the distance, wind and clouds thinning away.

sentences.zh: 屬時雨之新晴，觀百川之浩涆；

translations.literal: As fresh rain had just cleared, I viewed the hundred streams in vast flood;
translations.idiomatic: Fresh rain had just cleared, and I watched the hundred streams swell in flood;

sentences.zh: 水泓澄以暗夕，山參差而辨旦。

translations.literal: Waters were deep and clear toward dark evening; mountains unevenly distinct at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: the waters grew deep and clear toward evening, and the mountains stood jagged and distinct at dawn.

sentences.zh: 忽臨睨於故鄉，眇江天其無畔；

translations.literal: Suddenly I overlooked my old homeland from afar—river and sky boundless without shore;
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly I looked out over my old homeland—river and sky stretching away without end;

sentences.zh: 逆洄流而右阻，遵長薄而左貫。

translations.literal: Against the swirling current I was blocked on the right; following the long marsh I pierced through on the left.
translations.idiomatic: against the swirling current the right bank blocked my way, while on the left I threaded through the long marsh.

sentences.zh: 獨向風以舒情，搴芳洲其誰翫。

translations.literal: Alone I faced the wind to unburden my feelings; I plucked the fragrant islet—who else would share it?
translations.idiomatic: Alone I turned to the wind to ease my heart and plucked flowers on the fragrant islet—with whom could I share them?

sentences.zh: 息銅山而繫纜，訪叔文之靈宇；

translations.literal: I rested at Copper Mountain and tied my cable; I visited Shiwen's spirit hall;
translations.idiomatic: I moored at Copper Mountain and tied my cable, then visited the shrine of Shiwen;

sentences.zh: 得舊名而猶存，皆攢蕪而積楚。

translations.literal: Old names were still preserved—all overgrown with thorns and piled with brush.
translations.idiomatic: The old names still survived, but everything was choked with thorns and piled with wild brush.

sentences.zh: 想夫君之令問，實有聲於前古；

translations.literal: I thought of my lord's fine reputation—truly renowned in antiquity;
translations.idiomatic: I thought of that lord's fine reputation, truly famed in ancient times;

sentences.zh: 拯巴漢之廢業，爰配名於鄒魯。

translations.literal: He restored Ba and Han's ruined enterprise and thus matched the fame of Zou and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: he restored the ruined enterprise of Ba and Han and won a name to match those of Zou and Lu.

sentences.zh: 辨山精以息訟，對祠星而寤主。

translations.literal: He distinguished mountain spirits to end litigation and faced the Star of Sacrifice to awaken the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: He exposed mountain demons to end lawsuits and faced the Star of Sacrifice to awaken his lord.

sentences.zh: 每撫事以懷人，非末學其能睹。

translations.literal: Each time I touched these affairs to recall the man—not a shallow student could perceive this.
translations.idiomatic: Each time I touched these places to recall the man—only a shallow scholar could fail to see his worth.

sentences.zh: 嘉梅根之孝女，尚乘肥於媵姬；

translations.literal: I praise the filial daughter of Meigan—still riding a stout horse among concubines;
translations.idiomatic: I praise the filial daughter of Meigan, who still rode a fine horse among the concubines;

sentences.zh: 嗟吳人之重辟，憂峻網於將貽。

translations.literal: I sigh at the Wu people's heavy punishments and worry that the harsh net will soon ensnare.
translations.idiomatic: I grieve for the Wu people's harsh punishments and fear the tightening net about to fall.

sentences.zh: 彼沈瓜而顯義，指滄波而爲期；

translations.literal: That one sank melons to show righteousness and pointed to the vast waves as his pledge;
translations.idiomatic: One sank melons in the river to prove his righteousness and pointed to the vast waters as his pledge;

sentences.zh: 此浮履以明節，赴丹爓其何疑。

translations.literal: This one floated shoes to show integrity and rushed to the red flame—what hesitation could there be?
translations.idiomatic: another floated his shoes to prove his integrity and walked into the flames—what doubt could remain?

sentences.zh: 信理感而情悼，實悽悵於余悲；

translations.literal: Truly moved by principle and grieved in feeling—truly sorrowful in my sadness;
translations.idiomatic: Truly moved by their righteousness, I grieved in my heart and felt the full weight of sorrow;

sentences.zh: 空沈吟以遐想，愧邯鄲之妙詞。

translations.literal: Vainly I murmured in distant contemplation, ashamed before Handan's fine verses.
translations.idiomatic: I could only murmur in distant thought, ashamed before the fine verses of Handan Chun.

sentences.zh: 望南陵以寓目，美牙門之守志；

translations.literal: I gazed south toward Nanling for a view and praised Yamen's steadfast resolve;
translations.idiomatic: I looked south toward Nanling and praised the steadfast resolve of the gate commander;

sentences.zh: 當晉師之席捲，豈籓籬而不庇。

translations.literal: When Jin armies swept through—would a hedge not shelter?
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin armies swept through, would not even a hedge give shelter?

sentences.zh: 攜老弱於窮城，猶區區乎一簣。

translations.literal: Carrying old and weak in a besieged city, he still strove like one basket of earth.
translations.idiomatic: He sheltered old and weak in a doomed city and still struggled on, basket by basket.

sentences.zh: 雖挈瓶之小善，實君子之所識。

translations.literal: Though a small good like carrying a pitcher—it is truly what gentlemen recognize.
translations.idiomatic: Though it was a small deed, like carrying a pitcher of water, it is just what gentlemen honor.

sentences.zh: 闕一句是謂事人之禮。

translations.literal: A line is missing; this means the propriety of serving others.
translations.idiomatic: A line is missing; this means the propriety of serving others.

sentences.zh: 入雷池之長浦，想恭、岱之芳塵；

translations.literal: I entered Leichi's long inlet and thought of Gong and Dai's fragrant traces;
translations.idiomatic: I entered the long inlet of Leichi Pool and recalled the noble traces of Wang Gong and Wang Dai;

sentences.zh: 臨魚官以輟膳，踐寒蒲之抽筠。

translations.literal: At Fish Official I stopped my meal; I tread upon cold reeds with sprouting bamboo joints.
translations.idiomatic: At Fish Official I stopped to take my meal, treading cold reeds where fresh bamboo shoots had sprung up.

sentences.zh: 又有生爲令德，沒爲明神。

translations.literal: There were also those virtuous in life and bright spirits in death.
translations.idiomatic: There were also those who lived as models of virtue and became bright spirits after death.

sentences.zh: 或捐家事主，攜手拜親；

translations.literal: Some abandoned family to serve their lord, clasping hands to bow to their parents;
translations.idiomatic: Some abandoned their families to serve their lord, yet clasped hands in farewell to their parents;

sentences.zh: 或正身殉義，哀感市人。

translations.literal: Some straightened their bodies and died for righteousness—grief moved the market folk.
translations.idiomatic: Some gave their lives upright for righteousness, and their grief moved the people in the markets.

sentences.zh: 所以家稱純孝，國號能臣。

translations.literal: Therefore families called them pure filial; the state called them capable ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Thus their families called them models of filial piety, and the state called them able ministers.

sentences.zh: 揚清徽於上列，並異世而爲鄰。

translations.literal: They raised clear emblems among the upper ranks, from different ages yet neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: They raised bright banners among the honored dead, neighbors across different ages.

sentences.zh: 發曉渚而遡風，苦神吳之難習。

translations.literal: Setting out at dawn from the islet against the wind, bitter was Spirit Wu's current to master.
translations.idiomatic: I set out at dawn from the islet against the wind, struggling with the treacherous currents of Spirit Wu.

sentences.zh: 岸曜舟而不進，水騰沙以驚急。

translations.literal: Shores glittered but boats would not advance; water churned sand in startled urgency.
translations.idiomatic: The shores glittered yet the boats would not move forward; the waters churned the sand in sudden alarm.

sentences.zh: 天曀曀其垂陰，雨霏霏而來集；

translations.literal: Heaven dimly dim dropped its shade; rain fine fine came to gather;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven grew dim and lowered its shadow; fine rain came gathering in.

sentences.zh: 愍征夫之勞瘁，每搴帷而佇立。

translations.literal: Pitying the conscript laborers' toil and exhaustion, each time I lifted the curtain and stood waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by the laborers' weariness, I often drew back the curtain and stood watching.

sentences.zh: 由江沲之派別，望彭匯之通津，塗未中乎及絳，日已盈於浹旬。

translations.literal: Following the Jiang and Tuo where their branches parted, I looked toward Penghui's thoroughfare crossing; the road was not yet halfway to Jiang, yet the days had already filled a full ten-day span.
translations.idiomatic: Where the Jiang and Tuo divided their channels I looked toward the ferry crossing at Penghui; the journey was not yet half done, yet ten days had already passed.

sentences.zh: 於是千流共歸，萬嶺分狀；

translations.literal: Then a thousand streams flowed together in return, myriad peaks split into distinct forms;
translations.idiomatic: Then a thousand streams converged as one, myriad peaks unfolded in every shape;

sentences.zh: 倒影懸高，浮天瀉壯。

translations.literal: Inverted images hung high; the sky-floating expanse poured in majestic flood.
translations.idiomatic: Reflections hung high overhead; sky-floating waters poured forth in splendor.

sentences.zh: 清江洗滌，平湖夷暢；

translations.literal: The clear river washed and cleansed; the level lake lay open and smooth;
translations.idiomatic: The clear river washed all clean; the level lake spread smooth and wide;

sentences.zh: 飜光轉彩，出沒搖漾。

translations.literal: Light turned over and colors shifted; [things] appeared and vanished, swaying and rippling.
translations.idiomatic: Light wheeled and colors shifted; shadows rose and fell upon the swaying waves.

sentences.zh: 岷山、嶓冢，悠遠寂寥；

translations.literal: Min Mountain and Bozhong — far, remote, silent and empty;
translations.idiomatic: Min Mountain and Bozhong stood far off in lonely silence;

sentences.zh: 青湓、赤岸，控汐引潮。

translations.literal: Qingpen and Red Cliff controlled the ebb and drew the tide.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingpen and Red Cliff the currents mastered the tides and drew the flood.

sentences.zh: 望歸雲之蓊蓊，揚清風之飄飄；

translations.literal: I watched returning clouds lush and thick; the clear wind rose light and drifting;
translations.idiomatic: I watched homebound clouds mass in green profusion; a light breeze rose, drifting free;

sentences.zh: 界飛流於翠薄，耿長虹於青霄。

translations.literal: Marking flying streams upon emerald shallows; the bright long rainbow in the blue vault.
translations.idiomatic: Flying streams bound the green shallows; a bright rainbow spanned the azure sky.

sentences.zh: 若夫灌莽川涯，層潭水府，游泳之所往還，喧鳴之所攢聚。

translations.literal: As for the overgrown thickets on the river banks, layered pools and watery palaces — places where swimmers go and return, where clamorous cries gather and cluster.
translations.idiomatic: Then there were riverbanks overgrown with scrub, layered pools like watery palaces where swimmers came and went and clamor gathered in throngs.

sentences.zh: 群飛沙漲，掩薄草渚；

translations.literal: Flocks flying over sand bars, pressing close upon grassy islets;
translations.idiomatic: Birds flew in flocks above the sandbars, skimming the grassy shoals;

sentences.zh: 奇甲異鱗，雕文綷羽。

translations.literal: Strange armor and rare scales, carved patterns and clustered feathers.
translations.idiomatic: Creatures of strange shell and exotic scale, etched plumage in woven colors.

sentences.zh: 聽寡鶴之偏鳴，聞孤鴻之慕侶；

translations.literal: I heard a lone crane's solitary cry, heard a lone swan's longing for its mate;
translations.idiomatic: I heard a lone crane cry apart from the flock; I heard a solitary swan grieving for its mate;

sentences.zh: 在客行而多思，獨傷魂而悽楚。

translations.literal: Traveling as a guest with many thoughts, alone my spirit wounded and desolate.
translations.idiomatic: A guest on the road, my thoughts ran on; alone I mourned, my spirit broken with grief.

sentences.zh: 美中流之衝要，因習坎以守固。

translations.literal: Excellent is this midstream crossroads; relying upon Kan — the habit of water — to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Splendid is this mid-river choke point, fortified through the constant discipline of water's ways.

sentences.zh: 旣固之而設險，又居之而務德。

translations.literal: Having fortified it and set defenses, again dwelling there they pursued virtue.
translations.idiomatic: They fortified it with natural barriers and, dwelling there, cultivated virtue as well.

sentences.zh: 南通珠崖、夜郎，西款玉津、華墨。

translations.literal: South it connects Zhuya and Yelang; west it pays court at Yujin and Huamo.
translations.idiomatic: To the south it reaches Zhuya and Yelang; to the west it opens toward Yujin and Huamo.

sentences.zh: 莫不內清姦宄，外弭苛慝，籬屏京師，事有均於齊德也。

translations.literal: None failed inwardly to purge treachery and villainy, outwardly to still harsh cruelty — a hedge and screen for the capital; the deed equals the virtue of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Inwardly they cleared out treachery and villainy; outwardly they stilled harsh cruelty — a fence and shield for the capital, matching in deed the virtue of Qi.

sentences.zh: 眄匡嶺以躊躇，想霞裳於雲仞；

translations.literal: I gazed at Kuang Ridge and hesitated, thinking of cloud-robes upon cloud heights;
translations.idiomatic: I lingered gazing at Mount Lu, recalling immortals in cloud robes upon the cloud-crowned peaks;

sentences.zh: 流姮娥之逸響，發王子之清韻。

translations.literal: Floating Chang'e's lingering tones, releasing Prince Wang's pure notes.
translations.idiomatic: There floated Chang'e's lingering notes, and Wangzi's clear melody rose.

sentences.zh: 若夜光而可投，豈榮華之難擯。

translations.literal: If one could cast a night-pearl, how could glory and splendor be hard to cast aside?
translations.idiomatic: If a night-shining pearl could be offered up, how could glory be hard to renounce?

sentences.zh: 羨還丹其何術，佇一丸于來信。

translations.literal: I envied elixir's return — what art is there? — and waited for one pellet in a message to come.
translations.idiomatic: I wondered by what art one might refine the elixir, and waited for a single pellet borne in a letter from afar.

sentences.zh: 徑遵途乎鄂渚，迹孫氏之霸基；

translations.literal: The path led straight to Ezhu; I traced the Sun family's hegemonic foundation;
translations.idiomatic: The road ran straight to the isles of E; I traced the Sun clan's foundations of empire;

sentences.zh: 陳利兵而蓄粟，抗十倍之銳師。

translations.literal: They arrayed sharp weapons and stored grain, resisting an enemy ten times their strength in keen troops.
translations.idiomatic: They arrayed sharp weapons and hoarded grain, standing against a foe ten times their strength.

sentences.zh: 在賢才之必用，寧推誠而忍欺；

translations.literal: Since worthy talent must be employed, how much more to offer sincerity and forbear deception;
translations.idiomatic: When men of talent must be put to use, one would rather show sincerity than practice deceit;

sentences.zh: 圖富強以法立，屬貞臣而日嬉。

translations.literal: Plotting strength and wealth through established law, entrusting loyal ministers for daily counsel.
translations.idiomatic: They sought wealth and power through law, and daily entrusted themselves to loyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 識徐基於江畔，雲釣臺之舊址；

translations.literal: I recognized Xu Ji's site by the riverbank — the old location of Cloud Fishing Terrace;
translations.idiomatic: I recognized Xu Ji's legacy on the riverbank, the old site of the Fishing Terrace;

sentences.zh: 方戰國之多虞，猶從容而宴喜。

translations.literal: Even amid the Warring States' many perils, he still took ease at feasts and pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Even in the peril of the Warring States he still feasted at leisure in tranquil joy.

sentences.zh: 欽輔吳之忠諒，歎仲謀之虛己；

translations.literal: I admired those who aided Wu in loyalty and candor, sighed at Zhongmou's emptying himself;
translations.idiomatic: I honored those who served Wu with loyal candor and marveled at Sun Quan's humility before his men;

sentences.zh: 處君臣而並得，良致霸其有以。

translations.literal: Ruler and minister both obtained their due — truly this is how hegemony was achieved, and not without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and minister each had their place — no wonder he achieved the hegemony, and with good reason.

sentences.zh: 伊文侯之雅望，誠一代之偉人；

translations.literal: That Prince Wen — his elegant renown — truly a great man of an age;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wen, in his noble repute, was truly a great man of his generation;

sentences.zh: 禰觀書以心服，玉比德而譽均。

translations.literal: Mi Heng reading books submitted in heart; jade compared in virtue and fame equal.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng read and submitted his heart; men compared him to jade in virtue and equal renown.

sentences.zh: 遘時雄之應運，方協義以經綸；

translations.literal: Encountering a hero of the age who answered destiny's call, just then aligning with righteousness to order the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Meeting a hero of the age who answered Heaven's mandate, he was just then aligning with righteousness to order the realm;

sentences.zh: 名旣逼而愈賞，言雖聞而彌親。

translations.literal: Fame though pressing was ever more prized; words though heard grew ever more intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Though fame pressed close, it was prized all the more; though his words were heard abroad, intimacy only deepened.

sentences.zh: 惜勤王於延獻，俾漢京之惟新；

translations.literal: Alas, rallying troops for the throne at Yanxian, causing the Han capital to be renewed;
translations.idiomatic: Alas — he marched to aid the throne at Yanxian and made the Han capital new again;

sentences.zh: 何天命其弗與，悲盛業之未申。

translations.literal: Why did Heaven's mandate not grant it? — grieving that great enterprise was not fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Why did Heaven not grant him its mandate? I grieve that his great work was never fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 汎蘆洲以延佇，聞伍員之所濟；

translations.literal: I floated at Reed Isle and lingered long, hearing of Wu Yuan's crossing;
translations.idiomatic: I drifted at Reed Isle and lingered, thinking of Wu Zixu's crossing here;

sentences.zh: 出懷珠而免仇，歸投金以答惠。

translations.literal: Out with a pearl in the bosom to escape his foe; returning he cast gold to repay kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He fled with a pearl hidden in his bosom to escape his enemy, then returned and cast gold into the river to repay a kindness.

sentences.zh: 彼無求於萬鐘，唯長歌而鼓郐世；

translations.literal: He sought not ten thousand bells of grain; he only sang long and beat out the age of Kuai.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted no vast stipend — only to sing his grief and beat out the rhythm of a fallen age;

sentences.zh: 慨斯誠之未感，乃沈軀以明誓。

translations.literal: Grieved that such sincerity went unfelt, he then drowned his body to make his oath clear.
translations.idiomatic: Grieving that his sincerity went unheeded, he drowned himself to declare his vow.

sentences.zh: 空負恨其何追，徒臨飡而先祭；

translations.literal: Empty — resentment with nothing to pursue; in vain before the meal he was first mourned.
translations.idiomatic: What use is regret now? Nothing can be undone — men mourn him even before the feast begins;

sentences.zh: 及旋師於鄭國，美邀福於來裔。

translations.literal: When the army turned back at Zheng, beauty invited fortune upon later generations.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned from Zheng, he won blessing for generations to come;

sentences.zh: 入郢都而抵掌，壯天險之難窺；

translations.literal: Entering Ying's capital and clapping hands — how mighty the heaven-given barrier, hard to spy out.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital of Ying and laughed in triumph — how formidable its natural defenses had seemed;

sentences.zh: 允分荊之勝略，成百代之良規。

translations.literal: Truly the victorious strategy of dividing Jing — a fine plan for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: His strategy of partitioning Chu stands as a master plan for ages.

sentences.zh: 賈生方於指大，應侯譬之木披。

translations.literal: Jia Yi likened it to pointing at the larger; Marquis Ying compared it to splitting wood.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi compared it to pointing at what was already larger; Lord Ying likened it to cleaving wood along the grain.

sentences.zh: 所以居宗振末，強本弱枝，聞古今之通制，歷盛衰而不移，可不謂然與，美經國之遠體也。

translations.literal: Therefore establishing the trunk and invigorating the branches, strengthening the root and weakening the limbs — a universal rule through rise and fall unmoved — is this not so? — how beautiful the far-reaching body of statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: To hold the center firm and strengthen the branches, to fortify the root and weaken the limbs — this is the enduring law of ages, unchanged through rise and fall. Can one deny it? How fine is this fundamental principle of governing a state.

sentences.zh: 酌忠言於城郢，播終古之芳猷；

translations.literal: He poured loyal words at walled Ying, spreading fragrant plans through all antiquity;
translations.idiomatic: At the walls of Ying he offered loyal counsel, spreading a noble design through the ages;

sentences.zh: 忘我躬之匪閱，顧社稷而懷憂。

translations.literal: Forgetting himself in neglect of self, he turned to the altars of state and bore worry in his breast.
translations.idiomatic: He forgot himself and his own body, thinking only of the realm and its altars with worry in his heart.

sentences.zh: 服莊王之高義，乃征名於夏州；

translations.literal: Moved by King Zhuang's high righteousness, he was summoned by name from Xiazhou;
translations.idiomatic: Honoring King Zhuang's noble righteousness, Shen Zhu was summoned by name from Xia;

sentences.zh: 恥蹊田之過罰，納申叔之嘉謀。

translations.literal: Ashamed of excessive punishment for treading fields, he accepted Shen Shuqi's excellent counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of the harsh penalty for treading the fields, the king accepted Shen Shuqi's wise counsel.

sentences.zh: 觀巫臣之獻箴，鑒《周書》以明喻；

translations.literal: Observing Wuchen's presented admonition, mirroring the Zhou Documents for a clear parable;
translations.idiomatic: I recalled Wuchen's admonition and took the Book of Zhou as a clear mirror for his lesson;

sentences.zh: 何自謀其多僻，要桑中而遠赴。

translations.literal: Why did he plot so many crooked paths, insisting on Sangzhong and going far away?
translations.idiomatic: Why then did Wuchen scheme so crookedly, clinging to Sangzhong and fleeing to the distance?

sentences.zh: 若葆申之誅丹，實匡君以成務；

translations.literal: Like Bao Shen executing Dan — truly rectifying the lord to fulfill the task;
translations.idiomatic: Like Bao Shen when he executed the prince — truly reforming his lord to fulfill the state's work;

sentences.zh: 在兩臣而優劣，居二主其並裕。

translations.literal: Between the two ministers there was better and worse; under two lords both found abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Between the two ministers one sees strength and weakness; under two rulers both found their measure of success.

sentences.zh: 臨赤崖而慷愾，榷雄圖於魏武；

translations.literal: At Red Cliff I grew passionate, weighing the heroic plan of Wei Wu;
translations.idiomatic: At Red Cliff I stood inflamed with feeling, recalling the grand design of Cao Cao;

sentences.zh: 乘戰勝以長驅，志吞吳而幷楚。

translations.literal: Riding victory in long advance, his ambition swallowed Wu and annexed Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Riding on victory he drove forward, intent on swallowing Wu and merging with Chu.

sentences.zh: 總八州之毅卒，期姑蘇而振旅；

translations.literal: Gathering steadfast troops of eight provinces, he set his sights on Gusu and marshaled his army.
translations.idiomatic: He mustered resolute soldiers from eight provinces, aiming for Gusu to bring his army home in triumph.

sentences.zh: 時有便乎建瓴，事無留于蕭斧。

translations.literal: The moment favored pouring from a rooftop; affairs allowed no delay for the battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: The moment favored him as water poured from a high eave; nothing could stay the stroke of the axe.

sentences.zh: 霸孫赫其霆奮，杖邁俗之英輔；

translations.literal: Hegemon Sun blazed like thunder's leap; he leaned on helpers of talent beyond the common world;
translations.idiomatic: Hegemon Sun blazed forth like lightning; he relied on extraordinary ministers beyond the common run;

sentences.zh: 裂宇宙而三分，誠決機乎一舉。

translations.literal: He split the cosmos into three parts — truly deciding fate in a single move.
translations.idiomatic: He split the universe into three realms, truly deciding fate at one decisive stroke.

sentences.zh: 嗟玄德之矯矯，思興復於舊京；

translations.literal: Alas for Xuande's lofty bearing — thinking to restore the old capital;
translations.idiomatic: How lofty was Liu Bei, set on restoring the old capital;

sentences.zh: 招臥龍於當世，配管仲而稱英。

translations.literal: He recruited Sleeping Dragon in his age, matched Guan Zhong and was called a hero.
translations.idiomatic: He called Zhuge Liang from seclusion and was hailed as a hero worthy of Guan Zhong.

sentences.zh: 收散亡之餘弱，結與國而連橫，延五紀乎岷漢，紹四百於炎精。

translations.literal: He gathered scattered remnants and the weak, allied with neighboring states in linked counsels; extended five reign-periods at Min and Han, continued the four hundred years of the Fiery Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the scattered weak and made alliances abroad; for five reigns he held Min and Han, carrying on the four centuries of the Han mandate.

sentences.zh: 望巴丘以邅回，遵洞庭而敞恍，沉輕舟而不繫，何靈胥之浩蕩。

translations.literal: I looked toward Baling and turned winding back; followed Dongting and felt open and dazed; the light boat sank without mooring — how vast Spirit Wu's waters!
translations.idiomatic: I gazed toward Baling and wound back; following Dongting I felt dazed and open; the light boat drifts without mooring — how vast are the waters of Spirit Wu!

sentences.zh: 眺君、褊之雙峰，徒臨風以增想；

translations.literal: I gazed at the twin peaks of Jun and Bian — only facing the wind my thoughts increased;
translations.idiomatic: I gazed at the twin peaks of Jun and Bian, and facing the wind my longing only grew;

sentences.zh: 償瑤觴而一酌，駕彩蜺而獨往。

translations.literal: Repaying the jade cup with one draft, driving colored rainbows to go alone.
translations.idiomatic: I poured one libation from a jade cup and would ride the rainbow alone to go.

sentences.zh: 爾乃南奠衡、霍，北距沮、漳；

translations.literal: Then south it sets Heng and Huo; north it bars Ju and Zhang;
translations.idiomatic: South it reaches Mount Heng and Mount Huo; north it meets the Ju and Zhang rivers;

sentences.zh: 包括沅、澧，汲引瀟、湘。

translations.literal: It embraces Yuan and Li, draws and leads Xiao and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: It embraces the Yuan and Li rivers and draws up the Xiao and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 滮滮長邁，漫漫回翔；

translations.literal: Surging, surging — a long advance; vast, vast — wheeling flight;
translations.idiomatic: Waters surge and sweep far onward; vast and slow they wheel and soar;

sentences.zh: 蕩雲沃日，吐霞含光。

translations.literal: Swamping clouds and soaking the sun; spitting rosy mist and holding light.
translations.idiomatic: They drench the clouds and wash the sun; they breathe rosy mist and hold the light.

sentences.zh: 青碧潭嶼，萬頃澄澈；

translations.literal: Blue-green pools and islets — ten thousand acres clear and pure;
translations.idiomatic: Blue-green pools and islets span ten thousand acres of limpid clarity;

sentences.zh: 綺蘭從風，素沙被雪。

translations.literal: Orchid brocade follows the wind; white sand wears snow.
translations.idiomatic: Orchids lean in the wind like brocade; white sand wears a mantle of snow.

sentences.zh: 雜雲霞以舒卷，間河洲而斷絕；

translations.literal: Cloud and rosy light mingled in rolling spread; river islets between breaking off;
