translations.idiomatic: Cloud and sunset light rolled and unfurled together; river islets broke the view in fragments;

sentences.zh: 回曉仄於中川，起長飆而半滅。

translations.literal: Dawn light turned slanting in mid-river; a long gale rose and half extinguished it.
translations.idiomatic: Dawn slanted across midstream; a long wind rose and half put out the light.

sentences.zh: 稅遺構之舊浦，瞻汨羅以隕泗；

translations.literal: I moored at the old harbor of abandoned structures; gazed upon Miluo and tears fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: I moored at the old harbor of vanished ruins and looked upon the Miluo, where tears fall like rain;

sentences.zh: 豈懷寶而迷邦，猶殷勤而一致。

translations.literal: How could one harbor treasure and lose the state? — still earnest and of one mind.
translations.idiomatic: Had he truly cherished treasure and lost his way in the state? He remained earnest, single-minded to the end.

sentences.zh: 蘊芳華以襞積，非黨人之所媚；

translations.literal: Gathering fragrant bloom in layered folds — not for faction-men to flatter;
translations.idiomatic: His virtue layered like folded blossoms — not offered to flatter the factions;

sentences.zh: 合《小雅》之怨辭，兼《國風》之美志。

translations.literal: Combining the grievous words of the Lesser Odes with the beautiful intent of the Royal Odes.
translations.idiomatic: His laments joined the anguished verses of the Lesser Ya, and his spirit united the noble aims of the Kingdoms' Airs.

sentences.zh: 譬彈冠而振衣，猶自別於泥滓；

translations.literal: Like adjusting cap and shaking out robes — still setting himself apart from mud and filth;
translations.idiomatic: Like straightening one's cap and shaking out one's robe, he still kept himself apart from the mud;

sentences.zh: 且殺身以成義，寧露才而揚己？

translations.literal: Moreover to give the body for righteousness — how could he display talent and exalt himself?
translations.idiomatic: He gave his life to fulfill righteousness — would he rather display his talent and glorify himself?

sentences.zh: 悲先生之不辰，逢椒、蘭之妒美；

translations.literal: Grieving the Master's ill hour — encountering the envy's beauty of Pepper and Orchid;
translations.idiomatic: I grieve that the Master was born at the wrong time, facing the jealous beauty of Pepper and Orchid;

sentences.zh: 有驊騮而不馭，焉遑遑於千里。

translations.literal: Having a piebald steed yet not driving it — how could one hurry a thousand leagues?
translations.idiomatic: With a fine steed yet none to drive it, how could he race a thousand leagues?

sentences.zh: 旣踐境以思人，彌流連其無已。

translations.literal: Having entered the borders to think of the man, all the more I linger on without end.
translations.idiomatic: Having entered this land I think of him, and my lingering sorrow knows no end.

sentences.zh: 修行潦之薄薦，敢憑誠於沼沚。

translations.literal: Preparing a humble offering of gathered marsh reeds, I dare rely on sincerity at the pool and islet.
translations.idiomatic: I set out a humble offering gathered from the shallows, daring to offer my sincerity at the marshy shore.

sentences.zh: 謁黃陵而展敬，奠瑤席乎川湄。

translations.literal: I paid visit at Yellow Mounds and displayed reverence; laid jade mats at the river's edge.
translations.idiomatic: I visited the Yellow Mounds to pay reverence and laid jade mats on offerings at the river's edge.

sentences.zh: 具蘭香以膏沐，懷椒糈而要之。

translations.literal: I prepared orchid fragrance for anointing; in heart held peppered glutinous rice to invite them.
translations.idiomatic: I prepared orchid fragrance for ablution and bore peppered millet to summon the spirits.

sentences.zh: 延帝子於三後，降夔、龍於九疑。

translations.literal: I summoned the emperor's daughters to the Three Sovereigns; descended Kui and Long upon Jiuyi.
translations.idiomatic: I called the emperor's daughters and the Three Sovereigns, and summoned Kui and Long down from Jiuyi.

sentences.zh: 騰河靈之水駕，下太一之靈旗。

translations.literal: River Spirit rose upon water chariot; descended Grand One's spirit banners.
translations.idiomatic: The River Spirit soared on his watery chariot; the Spirit of Grand Unity lowered his sacred banners.

sentences.zh: 撫安歌以會儛，疏緩節而依遲。

translations.literal: I stroked the soothing song to meet the dance; loosened the slow beat and lingered long.
translations.idiomatic: I set the soothing song to the dance and eased the slow rhythm into lingering delay.

sentences.zh: 日徘徊以將暮，情眇默而無辭。

translations.literal: The sun wandered and would soon be dusk; feeling dim and silent without words.
translations.idiomatic: The sun loitered toward evening; my heart was still and mute, without words.

sentences.zh: 慍秦皇之巡幸，尤土壤以加戮；

translations.literal: Resenting Qin Shihuang's imperial tour — especially punishing the earth with executions;
translations.idiomatic: I resent Qin Shihuang's tour of the region, above all his slaughter of the land itself;

sentences.zh: 昧天道之無親，勤望祀以祈福。

translations.literal: Dark to Heaven's Way that shows no favor — he diligently made distant sacrifices to beg fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Blind to Heaven's impartial way, he busied himself with sacrifices on distant peaks to beg blessing.

sentences.zh: 將人怨而神怒，故飛川而蕩谷；

translations.literal: About to have men resentful and spirits wrathful — therefore rivers flew and valleys were scoured;
translations.idiomatic: When men resent and spirits rage, rivers burst forth and scour the valleys;

sentences.zh: 推冥理以歸諐，遂刊山而赭木。

translations.literal: Pushing dark principle back to guilt, he then cut mountains and reddened trees.
translations.idiomatic: He read into fate's dark design and laid the blame there; he carved the mountains and stained the trees red.

sentences.zh: 於是下車入部，班條理務，砥課庸薄，夕惕兢懼。

translations.literal: Then I alighted from the cart and entered the prefecture; sorted articles and ordered affairs; ground away the shallow and mean; evening vigilance, morning dread.
translations.idiomatic: Then I stepped down from my carriage and entered my command; I arranged policies and ordered affairs, tested the shallow and unworthy, and kept watch each night in anxious care.

sentences.zh: 存問長老，隱卹氓庶，奉宣皇恩，寬徭省賦。

translations.literal: Inquired after elders; secretly comforted the common folk; upheld and proclaimed royal grace; eased corvée and reduced levies.
translations.idiomatic: I visited the elders, comforted the people in their hidden grief, proclaimed the emperor's grace, and eased corvée and reduced taxes.

sentences.zh: 遠哉盛乎，斯邦之舊也。

translations.literal: Remote! Grand! — such is this realm's antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: How vast and how glorious is the ancient legacy of this land!

sentences.zh: 有虞巡方以託終，夏后開圖而疏決，太伯讓嗣以來遊，□臣祈仙而齊潔。

translations.literal: Shun on his tour of the regions entrusted his end here; Yu the Great opened the land chart and dredged the channels; Taibo yielded the succession and came to wander; [name lost] the minister prayed for immortality and kept pure rites.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shun toured the realm and ended his days here; Yu the Great opened the land and dredged the waters; Taibo yielded the throne and came to wander these shores; a minister, name lost to the text, prayed for immortality and kept pure rites.

sentences.zh: 固是明王之塵軌，聖賢之蹤轍也。

translations.literal: Truly these are dust-tracks of enlightened kings, footprint traces of sages and worthies.
translations.idiomatic: These are truly the dusty tracks of enlightened kings and the footfalls of sages and worthies.

sentences.zh: 若夫屈平《懷沙》之賦，賈子遊湘之篇，史遷摛文以投弔，揚雄《反騷》而沉川。

translations.literal: As for Qu Ping's 'Embracing the Sand' rhapsody, Master Jia's verses on wandering the Xiang, Sima Qian's spreading words to cast a memorial, and Yang Xiong's 'Counter-Sorrow' as he drowned in the river.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Qu Yuan's rhapsody "Embracing the Sand," Jia Yi's verses on the Xiang, Sima Qian's prose cast as a river offering, and Yang Xiong's "Counter-Sorrow," written as he went down into the stream.

sentences.zh: 其風謠雅什，又是詞人之所流連也。

translations.literal: Their wind-songs and elegant pieces are again what poets linger over.
translations.idiomatic: Their folk songs and elegant odes are what poets have lingered over ever since.

sentences.zh: 亦有仲寧、咸德，仍世相繼，父子三台，緇衣改敝。

translations.literal: There were also Zhongning and Xiande, succeeding generation after generation; father and son at the Three Platforms, black robes worn threadbare.
translations.idiomatic: There were Zhongning and Xiande as well, generation after generation in unbroken succession — father and son both reaching the Three Ducal Platforms, their black robes worn to rags from long service.

sentences.zh: 古初抱于烈火，劉先高而忤世，蔣公琰之弘通，桓柏緒之匡濟，鄧兗時之絕述，谷思恭之藻麗，實川嶽之精靈，常間出而無替也。

translations.literal: Gu Chu embraced in fierce fire; Liu Xiang high-minded and at odds with the age; Jiang Gongyan's broad mastery; Huan Boxu's rescue of the realm; Deng Kuanshi's unmatched writings; Gu Sigong's flowery elegance — truly spirits of rivers and mountains, ever appearing at intervals without decline.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Chu who embraced the flames; Liu Xiang, lofty and at odds with his age; Jiang Gongyan's broad mastery; Huan Boxu's saving of the realm; Deng Kuanshi's incomparable writings; Gu Sigong's ornate brilliance — truly the spirits of river and mountain, appearing again and again through the ages without fail.

sentences.zh: 至於殊庭之客，帝鄉之賢，神奔鬼化，吐吸雲煙。

translations.literal: As for guests of the wondrous court and worthies of the emperor's homeland — spirits racing, ghosts transforming, breathing in and out cloud and mist.
translations.idiomatic: Then there are the guests of the wondrous courts and the worthies of the immortals' realm — spirits in flight, ghosts transfigured, inhaling and exhaling cloud and mist.

sentences.zh: 玉笥登之而卻老，金人植杖以尊泉，蘇生騎龍而出入，處靜駕鹿以周旋。

translations.literal: Yuqie ascended it and turned back old age; the golden man planted his staff to honor the spring; Master Su rode a dragon in coming and going; Chujing drove a deer in his comings and goings.
translations.idiomatic: On Mount Yuqie one climbs and turns back old age; the golden man planted his staff to honor the sacred spring; Master Su rode a dragon to and fro; Chujing drove a deer as he moved through the world.

sentences.zh: 配北燭之神女，偶南榮之偓佺。

translations.literal: He matched the goddess of North Zhu; he paired with Wonuo of Nanrong.
translations.idiomatic: He took as consort the goddess of North Zhu; he joined with Wonuo of Nanrong.

sentences.zh: 時髣髴其遙見，亦往往而有焉。

translations.literal: At times one dimly sees them from afar; they too appear now and again.
translations.idiomatic: At times one seems to glimpse them from afar; they appear here and there even now.

sentences.zh: 爾乃歷省府庭，周行街術，山川遠覽，邑居近悉。

translations.literal: Then I passed through the provincial offices and courtyards, walked all the streets and lanes, gazed far upon mountains and rivers, and knew the nearby settlements intimately.
translations.idiomatic: Then I toured the provincial offices and halls, walked every street and lane, looked far over mountains and rivers, and came to know the nearby towns in full detail.

sentences.zh: 割黔中以置守，獻青陽而背質，鄒生所謂還舟，楚王於焉乘馹。

translations.literal: Qianzhong was carved off to set guards; Qingyang was offered and the pledge turned back; the returning boat of which Master Zou spoke — here the King of Chu took post relays.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhong was carved away to establish garrisons; Qingyang was offered and the pledge reversed; here was the "returning boat" of which Zou Yan spoke, and here the King of Chu took the post relays.

sentences.zh: 巡高山之累仞，褒吳文之爲宰；

translations.literal: I toured mountains piled many ren high, and praised Wu Wen as minister;
translations.idiomatic: I climbed mountains piled many ren high, and praised Wu Wen's service as minister;

sentences.zh: 彼非劉而八王，皆國亡而身醢。

translations.literal: Those eight princes who were not Liu — all lost their states and were minced to paste.
translations.idiomatic: those eight princes of the Sima clan — all lost their states and were minced to paste.

sentences.zh: 在長沙而著令，經五葉其未改；

translations.literal: Laws were established in Changsha, and through five generations they were unchanged;
translations.idiomatic: Laws were established in Changsha and held unchanged through five generations;

sentences.zh: 知天道之福謙，勝一時之經始。

translations.literal: Knowing that Heaven's Way blesses humility, better than a moment's founding enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: knowing that Heaven's Way blesses humility — a lesson better than any moment's founding enterprise.

sentences.zh: 尋太傅之故宅，今築室以安禪；

translations.literal: I sought the Grand Tutor's old residence; now a chamber is built there for quiet meditation;
translations.idiomatic: I sought the Grand Tutor's old residence, where now a chamber has been built for quiet meditation;

sentences.zh: 邑無改于舊井，尚開流而冽泉。

translations.literal: The settlement unchanged from its old wells — still a flowing spring, cold and clear.
translations.idiomatic: the settlement unchanged from its old wells, where a cold, clear spring still flows.

sentences.zh: 懷伊、管之政術，遇庸臣而見遷；

translations.literal: Cherishing the governance of Yi and Guan, yet meeting mediocre ministers and being transferred away;
translations.idiomatic: He cherished the governance of Yi Yin and Guan Zhong, yet met mediocre ministers and was transferred away;

sentences.zh: 終被知於時主，嗟漢宗之得賢。

translations.literal: At last recognized by the ruler of the age — ah, how the House of Han gained a worthy man.
translations.idiomatic: at last he won recognition from the ruler of the age — how fortunate the House of Han was to gain such a man.

sentences.zh: 受齊君之遠託，豈理謝而生全；

translations.literal: Receiving the distant trust of the Lord of Qi — how could reason fail and life be preserved;
translations.idiomatic: He received the distant trust of the Lord of Qi — how could reason fail and life be preserved?

sentences.zh: 哀懷王之不秀，遂抱恨而傷年。

translations.literal: Grieving King Huai's lack of excellence, he thus nursed resentment and shortened his years.
translations.idiomatic: Grieving King Huai's lack of excellence, he nursed resentment and shortened his years.

sentences.zh: 脩定祀于北郭，對林野而幽藹；

translations.literal: He restored fixed sacrifices at the north suburb, facing forest and wild in dim seclusion;
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices were restored at the north suburb, facing forest and wild in dim seclusion;

sentences.zh: 庶無吐于馨香，祀瓊茅而沃酹。

translations.literal: Hoping for no taint upon the fragrant offering, he sacrificed with jade grass and poured libation.
translations.idiomatic: hoping the fragrant offering would remain untainted, he sacrificed with jade grass and poured libation.

sentences.zh: 景十三以啓國，惟君王其能大；

translations.literal: King Jing, thirteenth of the line, opened the state — only a prince could enlarge it thus;
translations.idiomatic: King Jing, thirteenth of the line, opened the state — only such a prince could enlarge it;

sentences.zh: 迨炎正之中微，實斯籓而是賴。

translations.literal: When the flame of Han declined midway, this fief alone was truly relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: when the flame of Han declined midway, this fief alone was truly relied upon.

sentences.zh: 顧四阜之紆餘，乍升高以遊目；

translations.literal: I looked back at the winding four hills, then suddenly climbed high to let my gaze roam;
translations.idiomatic: Turning to the winding four hills, I suddenly climbed high and let my gaze roam;

sentences.zh: 審山川之面帶，將取名於衡麓。

translations.literal: I examined how mountains and rivers gird the land, and would take my name from Heng's foothills.
translations.idiomatic: I examined how mountains and rivers gird the land, and would take my name from the foothills of Mount Heng.

sentences.zh: 下彌漫以爽塏，上欽虧而重復；

translations.literal: Below, broad and open and bright; above, peaks bowing and folding in layers;
translations.idiomatic: Below, all was broad, open, and bright; above, peaks bowed and folded in layers;

sentences.zh: 風瑟瑟以鳴松，水琤琤而響谷。

translations.literal: Wind soughs and sighs among the pines; water chimes and rings through the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: The wind soughs and sighs among the pines; water chimes and rings through the valleys.

sentences.zh: 低四照於若華，竦千尋於建木。

translations.literal: It lowers the fourfold radiance of Ruohua; it lifts a thousand fathoms toward the Jian Tree.
translations.idiomatic: Below lay the fourfold radiance of Ruohua; above rose a thousand fathoms toward the Jian Tree.

sentences.zh: 冀囂塵之可屏，登岩阿而寤宿。

translations.literal: I hoped the clamor of dust could be screened out, and climbed the cliff-side to wake and lodge.
translations.idiomatic: I hoped the clamor of the world could be shut out, and climbed the cliff-side to wake and lodge there.

sentences.zh: 舍域中之常戀，慕遊仙之靈族。

translations.literal: I set aside the common longing of the realm and yearned for the spirit-clan of wandering immortals.
translations.idiomatic: I set aside the world's common longing and yearned for the spirit-clan of wandering immortals.

sentences.zh: 是時涼風暮節，萬實西成，華池迥遠，飛閣淒明。

translations.literal: At that time the cool wind marked the evening of the season; ten thousand fruits ripened in the west; the flower-pool stretched far away; flying pavilions stood clear and chill.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the cool wind marked the season's evening; ten thousand fruits ripened in the west; the flower-pool stretched far away; flying pavilions stood clear and chill.

sentences.zh: 嘉南州之炎德，愛蘭蕙之秋榮。

translations.literal: I praised the southern land's blazing virtue and loved the orchids' and irises' autumn glory.
translations.idiomatic: I praised the southern land's blazing virtue and loved the autumn glory of orchids and irises.

sentences.zh: 下名柑於曲榭，采芳菊於高城。

translations.literal: Below, famous oranges at the winding pavilion; above, I gathered fragrant chrysanthemums on the high wall.
translations.idiomatic: Below, I tasted famous oranges at the winding pavilion; above, I gathered fragrant chrysanthemums on the high wall.

sentences.zh: 樹羅軒而並列，竹被嶺而叢生。

translations.literal: Trees lined the galleries side by side; bamboo covered the ridge in clustered growth.
translations.idiomatic: Trees lined the galleries in rows; bamboo covered the ridge in clustered growth.

sentences.zh: 翫棲禽之夕返，送旅雁之晨征。

translations.literal: I watched roosting birds return at evening and sent off migrating geese on the morning journey.
translations.idiomatic: I watched roosting birds return at dusk and saw migrating geese depart at dawn.

sentences.zh: 悲去鄉而遠客，寄覽物而娛情。

translations.literal: Grieving one who left home as a distant guest, I entrusted my feelings to viewing things for solace.
translations.idiomatic: Grieving one far from home, I entrusted my feelings to the things I viewed for solace.

sentences.zh: 惟傳車之所騖，實鷹揚其是掌，或解組以立威，乍露服而加賞。

translations.literal: Only the relay carriage's rushing course — truly the hawk's soaring is what the hand holds; sometimes one removes the seal-cord to establish authority, sometimes one briefly bares humble dress and receives reward.
translations.idiomatic: Where the relay carriage rushes on its course — truly the hawk's soaring is what the hand holds; sometimes one removes the seal-cord to establish authority, sometimes one briefly bares humble dress and receives reward.

sentences.zh: 遵聖主之恩刑，荷天地之厚德。

translations.literal: I follow the sage ruler's grace and punishment; I bear Heaven and Earth's thick virtue.
translations.idiomatic: I follow the sage ruler's grace and punishment and bear Heaven and Earth's thick virtue.

sentences.zh: 沾河潤於九里，澤自家而刑國。

translations.literal: River-moisture reaches nine li; grace spreads from the household to govern the state.
translations.idiomatic: Like river-moisture reaching nine li, grace spreads from the household to govern the state.

sentences.zh: 闕小道之可觀，寧畏塗其易克；

translations.literal: I leave aside the petty path that may be viewed — better to fear a road easy to traverse;
translations.idiomatic: I leave aside the petty path that may be viewed — I would rather fear a road easy to traverse;

sentences.zh: 眄高衢而願騁，憂取累於長纆。

translations.literal: I glance at the high thoroughfare and wish to gallop free, yet worry of being tethered by a long lead.
translations.idiomatic: I glance at the high thoroughfare and wish to gallop free, yet fear being tethered by a long lead.

sentences.zh: 聞困石之非據，承炯戒乎明則；

translations.literal: I have heard that a troubled stone is no fit seat; I receive the bright warning of the clear rule;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that a troubled stone is no fit seat; I take the bright warning of the clear rule;

sentences.zh: 愧壽陵之餘子，學邯鄲而匍匐也。

translations.literal: Ashamed as Shouling's leftover son, I study Handan and crawl on all fours.
translations.idiomatic: Like Shouling's leftover son, ashamed, I study Handan and crawl on all fours.

sentences.zh: 纘至州，停遣十郡慰勞，解放老疾吏役，及關市戍邏先所防人，一皆省併。

translations.literal: When Zuan reached the province, he halted and sent envoys to ten commanderies to offer comfort; he released aged and infirm clerks and corvée laborers, and all market-guard and frontier garrison personnel previously posted — all were reduced and merged.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuan reached the province, he halted his progress and sent envoys to ten commanderies to offer comfort; he released aged and infirm clerks and corvée laborers, and consolidated all market guards, frontier garrisons, and previously posted personnel.

sentences.zh: 州界零陵、衡陽等郡，有莫徭蠻者，依山險爲居，歷政不賓服，因此向化。

translations.literal: Within the province's borders, in commanderies such as Lingling and Hengyang, there were Mo Yao barbarians who dwelled in mountain fastnesses; through successive administrations they had not submitted, but now because of this they turned toward civilization.
translations.idiomatic: Within the province, in commanderies such as Lingling and Hengyang, Mo Yao tribesmen lived in mountain fastnesses; through successive administrations they had not submitted, but now they turned toward civilization.

sentences.zh: 益陽縣人作田二頃，皆異畝同穎。

translations.literal: People of Yiyang County planted fields of two qing, and every plot bore identical ears of grain.
translations.idiomatic: In Yiyang County people planted fields of two qing, and every separate plot bore identical ears of grain.

sentences.zh: 纘在政四年，流人自歸，戶口增益十餘萬，州境大安。

translations.literal: Zuan governed for four years; displaced people returned of themselves; registered households increased by more than a hundred thousand; the province's territory was greatly at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan governed for four years; displaced people returned of their own accord; registered households increased by more than a hundred thousand; and the province was greatly at peace.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，徵爲領軍，俄改授使持節、都督雍梁北秦東益郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡諸軍事、平北將軍、寧蠻校尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing he was summoned as Commander of the Palace Guard; shortly afterward he was reassigned Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander over the military affairs of Yong, Liang, Northern Qin, Eastern Yi, Jingzhou's Jingling, and Sizhou's Suicommandery, General Who Pacifies the North, and Colonel Pacifying the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiqing he was summoned as Commander of the Palace Guard; shortly afterward he was reassigned Bearer of the Staff of Authority, with command over Yong, Liang, Northern Qin, Eastern Yi, Jingzhou's Jingling, and Sizhou's Suicommandery, as General Who Pacifies the North and Colonel Pacifying the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 纘初聞邵陵王綸當代己爲湘州，其後定用河東王譽，纘素輕少王，州府候迎及資待甚薄，譽深銜之。

translations.literal: Zuan at first heard that Prince Shaoling Lun would replace him as Governor of Xiangzhou; afterward it was settled that Prince of Hedong Yu would be appointed. Zuan had always looked down on the young prince; the provincial offices' welcome and supplies were very meager, and Yu deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zuan heard that Prince Shaoling Lun would replace him as Governor of Xiangzhou; afterward Prince of Hedong Yu was appointed instead. Zuan had always looked down on the young prince, and the provincial offices' welcome and provisions were very meager — Yu deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 及至州，遂託疾不見纘，仍檢括州府庶事，留纘不遣。

translations.literal: When Yu reached the province, he feigned illness and refused to see Zuan; he still inspected and took account of the provincial offices' various affairs, and detained Zuan without sending him away.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu reached the province he feigned illness and refused to see Zuan; he inspected and took account of the provincial offices' affairs and detained Zuan without sending him on.

sentences.zh: 會聞侯景寇京師，譽飾裝當下援，時荊州刺史湘東王赴援，軍次郢州武城，纘馳信報曰：「河東已豎檣上水，將襲荊州。

translations.literal: It happened that word came that Hou Jing was raiding the capital; Yu prepared to go downstream in relief. At that time the Governor of Jingzhou, the Prince of Xiangdong, was hurrying to the rescue; his army halted at Wucheng in Ezhou. Zuan urgently sent word saying: "The Prince of Hedong has already raised sails upstream and is about to attack Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that word came Hou Jing was raiding the capital; Yu prepared to go downstream in relief. At that time the Governor of Jingzhou, the Prince of Xiangdong, was hurrying to the rescue, his army halting at Wucheng in Ezhou. Zuan urgently sent word saying: "The Prince of Hedong has already raised sails upstream and is about to attack Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 」王信之，便回軍鎮，荊、湘因構嫌隙。

translations.literal: " The prince believed it and at once turned his army back to garrison; Jing and Xiang thus bred mutual suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince believed it, turned his army back to garrison, and Jing and Xiang thus bred mutual suspicion.

sentences.zh: 尋棄其部伍，單舸赴江陵，王卽遣使責讓譽，索纘部下。

translations.literal: Before long Yu abandoned his troops, took a lone boat to Jiangling; the prince immediately sent an envoy to rebuke Yu and demand Zuan's subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yu abandoned his troops and took a lone boat to Jiangling; the prince immediately sent an envoy to rebuke Yu and demand Zuan's subordinates.

sentences.zh: 旣至，仍遣纘向襄陽，前刺史岳陽王察推遷未去鎮，但以城西白馬寺處之。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he still sent Zuan toward Xiangyang; the former Governor, Prince of Yueyang Cha, had deferred transfer and not yet left his post, but only lodged him at White Horse Temple west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu arrived, he still sent Zuan toward Xiangyang; the former Governor, Prince of Yueyang Cha, had deferred transfer and not yet left his post, but only lodged him at White Horse Temple west of the city.

sentences.zh: 會聞賊陷京師，詧因不受代。

translations.literal: It happened that word came the bandits had taken the capital; Cha therefore refused to accept replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Word then came that the bandits had taken the capital; Cha therefore refused to accept replacement.

sentences.zh: 州助防杜岸紿纘曰：「觀岳陽殿下必不容使君，使君素得物情，若走入西山，招聚義衆，遠近必當投集，又帥部下繼至，以此義舉，無往不克。

translations.literal: The provincial aide Du An deceived Zuan, saying: "Judging by it, Prince Yueyang will surely not tolerate the Governor. The Governor has always won the people's hearts; if you flee into the western hills and gather a righteous host, those near and far will surely rally to you. When your subordinates follow in succession, with such a righteous rising nothing will fail.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial aide Du An deceived Zuan, saying: "From what I can see, Prince Yueyang will surely not tolerate the Governor. The Governor has always won the people's hearts; if you flee into the western hills and gather a righteous host, those near and far will surely rally to you. When your subordinates follow in succession, with such a righteous rising nothing will fail.

sentences.zh: 」纘信之，與結盟約，因夜遁入山。

translations.literal: " Zuan believed him, formed a covenant with him, and by night fled into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: " Zuan believed him, formed a covenant, and by night fled into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 岸反以告詧，仍遣岸帥軍追纘。

translations.literal: An instead reported this to Cha and still sent An leading troops in pursuit of Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: An instead reported this to Cha and sent An leading troops in pursuit of Zuan.

sentences.zh: 纘衆望岸軍大喜，謂是赴期，旣至，卽執纘並其衆，並俘送之。

translations.literal: Zuan's followers saw An's army and rejoiced greatly, thinking they had arrived on schedule; once they came near, they at once seized Zuan together with his followers and sent them captive.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's followers saw An's army and rejoiced greatly, thinking help had arrived on schedule; once they came near, they seized Zuan together with his followers and sent them captive.

sentences.zh: 始被囚縶，尋又逼纘剃髮爲道人。

translations.literal: At first he was imprisoned and bound; soon afterward they also forced Zuan to shave his head and become a Daoist priest.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was imprisoned and bound; soon afterward they forced Zuan to shave his head and become a Daoist priest.

sentences.zh: 其年，詧舉兵襲江陵，常載纘隨後。

translations.literal: That year Cha raised troops and attacked Jiangling, always carrying Zuan along behind.
translations.idiomatic: That year Cha raised troops and attacked Jiangling, always keeping Zuan with him.

sentences.zh: 及軍退敗，行至湕水南，防守纘者慮追兵至，遂害之，棄尸而去，時年五十一。

translations.literal: When the army retreated in defeat and reached the south bank of the Jianshui, those guarding Zuan feared pursuing troops would arrive; they therefore killed him and abandoned the corpse and left. He was fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: When the army retreated in defeat and reached the south bank of the Jianshui, those guarding Zuan feared pursuing troops would arrive; they killed him, abandoned the corpse, and fled. He was fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 元帝承制，贈纘侍中、中衛將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan, acting on imperial authority, posthumously awarded Zuan Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Central Guard, and Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon with the same ceremonial honors as the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan, acting on imperial authority, posthumously awarded Zuan Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Central Guard, and the ceremonial honors of Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 諡簡憲公。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Duke Jianxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Duke Jianxian.

sentences.zh: 纘有識鑒，自見元帝，便推誠委結。

translations.literal: Zuan had discernment; from the time he met Emperor Yuan he offered sincere trust and close alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan had discernment; from the time he met Emperor Yuan he gave him sincere trust and close alliance.

sentences.zh: 及元帝卽位，追思之，嘗爲詩，其《序》曰：「簡憲之爲人也，不事王侯，負才任氣，見余則申旦達夕，不能已已。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan took the throne, he recalled him fondly and once composed a poem; its Preface says: "Jianxian as a man did not serve kings and lords, relied on talent and bore his spirit proudly; when he saw me he would talk from dawn till dusk without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan took the throne he recalled him fondly and once composed a poem; its Preface says: "Jianxian as a man did not serve kings and lords; he relied on talent and bore his spirit proudly. When he saw me he would talk from dawn till dusk without cease.

sentences.zh: 懷夫人之德，何日忘之。

translations.literal: How could I ever forget such a man's kindness?
translations.idiomatic: How could I ever forget a kindness such as his?

sentences.zh: 」纘著《鴻寶》一百卷，文集二十卷。

translations.literal: " Zuan wrote Hongbao in one hundred scrolls and a collected works in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: " Zuan wrote the Hongbao in one hundred scrolls and a collected works in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 次子希，字子顏，早知名，選尚太宗第九女海鹽公主。

translations.literal: His second son Xi, styled Ziyan, was early known by reputation; he was selected to marry the ninth daughter of Emperor Taizong, Princess Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Xi, styled Ziyan, was known early for his reputation; he was selected to marry the ninth daughter of Emperor Taizong, Princess Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 承聖初，官至黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chengsheng era he reached the office of Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chengsheng era he rose to the office of Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 綰字孝卿，纘第四弟也。

translations.literal: Wan, styled Xiaoqing, was Zuan's fourth younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Wan, styled Xiaoqing, was the fourth younger brother of Zuan.

sentences.zh: 初爲國子生，射策高第。

translations.literal: At first he was a student at the Imperial Academy and ranked high in the archery-and-essay examination.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered the Imperial Academy as a student and ranked high in the archery-and-essay examination.

sentences.zh: 起家長兼秘書郎，遷太子舍人，洗馬，中舍人，並掌管記。

translations.literal: He began his career as Senior Concurrent Secretary of the Masters of Writing, was transferred to Attendant of the Heir Apparent, Groom, and Household Attendant of the Heir Apparent — all while managing the records.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Senior Concurrent Secretary of the Masters of Writing, then was transferred to Attendant of the Heir Apparent, Groom, and Household Attendant of the Heir Apparent — all while managing the records.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書郎，國子博士。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Gentleman of the Secretariat and Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to Gentleman of the Secretariat and Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 出爲北中郎長史、蘭陵太守，還除員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Chief Administrator to the North General of the Army and Administrator of Lanling; on return he was appointed Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Chief Administrator to the North General of the Army and Administrator of Lanling; on return he was made Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 時丹陽尹西昌侯蕭淵藻以久疾未拜，敕綰權知尹事，遷中軍宣城王長史，俄徙御史中丞。

translations.literal: At that time the Intendant of Danyang, Marquis of Xichang Xiao Yuanzao, because of long illness had not yet taken office; the emperor ordered Wan to act provisionally in the Intendant's affairs. He was transferred to Chief Administrator to the Prince of Xuancheng's Central Army, and shortly afterward moved to Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Intendant of Danyang, Marquis of Xichang Xiao Yuanzao, because of long illness had not yet taken office; the emperor ordered Wan to act provisionally as Intendant. He was transferred to Chief Administrator to the Prince of Xuancheng's Central Army, and shortly afterward became Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣其弟中書舍人絢宣旨曰：「爲國之急，惟在執憲直繩，用人本不限升降。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent his younger brother, Palace Attendant Xuan, to proclaim the imperial will, saying: "What is urgent for the state lies solely in holding the law straight and true; in employing men the root principle is not to limit by rank high or low.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent his younger brother, Palace Attendant Xuan, to proclaim the imperial will, saying: "The state's urgent need lies solely in holding the law straight and true; in employing men the root principle is not to limit by rank high or low.

sentences.zh: 晉宋之世，周閔、蔡廓並以侍中爲之，卿勿疑是左遷也。

translations.literal: In the Jin and Song ages, Zhou Min and Cai Kuo both held the post while serving as Attendants-in-Ordinary — do not suspect this is a lateral demotion.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jin and Song ages, Zhou Min and Cai Kuo both held the post while serving as Attendants-in-Ordinary — you need not suspect this is a lateral demotion.

sentences.zh: 」時宣城王府望重，故有此旨焉。

translations.literal: " At that time the Prince of Xuancheng's establishment carried heavy prestige; hence this decree.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time the Prince of Xuancheng's establishment carried heavy prestige; hence this decree was issued.

sentences.zh: 大同四年元日，舊制僕射中丞坐位東西相當，時綰兄纘爲僕射，及百司就列，兄弟導騶，分趨兩陛，前代未有也，時人榮之。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the fourth year of Datong, by old regulation the Vice Director and Imperial Censor sat east and west as equals; at that time Wan's elder brother Zuan was Vice Director, and when the hundred offices took their places the brothers' outriders led the way and they parted toward the two staircases — nothing like it in former ages; men of the time honored them.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the fourth year of Datong, by old regulation the Vice Director and Imperial Censor sat east and west as equals. At that time Wan's elder brother Zuan was Vice Director; when the hundred offices took their places, the brothers' outriders led the way and they parted toward the two staircases — nothing like it in former ages, and men of the time honored them.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，出爲豫章內史。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was sent out as Internal Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was sent out to serve as Internal Administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 綰在郡，述《制旨禮記正言》義，四姓衣冠士子聽者常數百人。

translations.literal: While Wan was in the commandery he expounded the meaning of the Imperially Endorsed Correct Words on the Book of Rites; gentry of the four surname-clans and scholars who came to listen often numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: While governing the commandery Wan lectured on the meaning of the Imperially Endorsed Correct Words on the Book of Rites; gentry of the four surname-clans and scholars who came to listen often numbered several hundred.

sentences.zh: 八年，安成人劉敬宮挾祅道，遂聚黨攻郡，內史蕭侻棄城走。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Liu Jinggong of Ancheng embraced heterodox teachings and gathered a band to attack the commandery; the Internal Administrator Xiao Tuo abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, Liu Jinggong of Ancheng embraced heterodox teachings and gathered a band to attack the commandery; Internal Administrator Xiao Tuo abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 賊轉寇南康、廬陵，屠破縣邑，有衆數萬人，進寇豫章新淦縣。

translations.literal: The bandits turned to raid Nankang and Luling, slaughtered and destroyed counties and towns, had a host of several tens of thousands, and advanced to raid Xingan County in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits turned to raid Nankang and Luling, slaughtering and destroying counties and towns; they mustered several tens of thousands and advanced to raid Xingan County in Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 南中久不習兵革，吏民恇擾奔散。

translations.literal: The south-central region had long been unused to war; officials and people panicked and scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: The south-central region had long been unused to war, and officials and people panicked and scattered in flight.

sentences.zh: 或勸綰宜避其鋒，綰不從，仍修城隍，設戰備，募召敢勇，得萬餘人。

translations.literal: Some advised Wan that he ought to avoid their sharp edge; Wan would not follow, but still repaired walls and moats, set battle preparations, and recruited the bold — obtaining more than ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Some advised Wan to avoid their sharp edge, but Wan would not follow; he repaired walls and moats, set battle preparations, and recruited the bold — obtaining more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 刺史湘東王遣司馬王僧辯帥兵討賊，受綰節度，旬月間，賊黨悉平。

translations.literal: The Governor, the Prince of Xiangdong, sent Chief Administrator Wang Sengbian leading troops to suppress the bandits; he accepted Wan's command, and within a month the bandit faction was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Governor, the Prince of Xiangdong, sent Chief Administrator Wang Sengbian with troops to suppress the bandits; he accepted Wan's command, and within a month the bandit faction was entirely pacified.

sentences.zh: 十年，復爲御史中丞，加通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he again became Imperial Censor, with the added title Supernumerary Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he again took up the censorate, with the added title Supernumerary Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 綰再爲憲司，彈糾無所回避，豪右憚之。

translations.literal: Wan twice held the censorate; in impeachment and correction he avoided nothing; the powerful and great feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Wan twice held the censorate; in impeachment and correction he avoided nothing, and the powerful and great feared him.

sentences.zh: 是時城西開士林館聚學者，綰與右衛朱异、太府卿賀琛遞述《制旨禮記中庸》義。

translations.literal: At that time west of the city the Forest of Scholars Hall was opened to gather scholars; Wan together with Right Guard Zhu Yi and Minister of the Palace Granary He Chen expounded in turn the meaning of the Imperially Endorsed Doctrine of the Mean in the Book of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At that time west of the city the Forest of Scholars Hall was opened to gather scholars; Wan together with Right Guard Zhu Yi and Minister of the Palace Granary He Chen lectured in turn on the meaning of the Imperially Endorsed Doctrine of the Mean in the Book of Rites.

sentences.zh: 太清二年，遷左衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing he was transferred to General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiqing he was transferred to the post of General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 會侯景寇至，入守東掖門。

translations.literal: It happened that Hou Jing raided up to the capital; he entered to hold the Eastern Side Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing raided up to the capital, Wan entered to hold the Eastern Side Gate.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Minister of the Personnel Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to the post of Minister of the Personnel Section.

sentences.zh: 宮城陷，綰出奔，外轉至江陵。

translations.literal: When the palace city fell, Wan fled outward and eventually reached Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace city fell, Wan fled outward and eventually made his way to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 湘東王承制，授侍中、左衛將軍、相國長史，侍中如故。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiangdong, acting on imperial authority, appointed him Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Left Guard, and Chief Administrator to the Chancellor — Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiangdong, acting on imperial authority, appointed him Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Left Guard, and Chief Administrator to the Chancellor, retaining Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.

sentences.zh: 出爲持節、雲麾將軍、湘東內史。

translations.literal: He was sent out Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General of the Cloud Pennant, and Internal Administrator of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General of the Cloud Pennant, and Internal Administrator of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 承聖二年，徵爲尚書右僕射，尋加侍中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng he was summoned as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and shortly afterward was given the added title Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chengsheng he was summoned as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; shortly afterward he was given the added title Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 明年，江陵陷，朝士皆俘入關，綰以疾免，後卒於江陵，時年六十三。

translations.literal: The next year Jiangling fell; court gentlemen were all taken captive into the north. Wan was excused because of illness; afterward he died at Jiangling. He was sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Jiangling fell; court gentlemen were all taken captive into the north. Wan was excused because of illness and afterward died at Jiangling. He was sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 次子交，字少遊，頗涉文學，選尚太宗第十一女安陽公主。

translations.literal: His second son Jiao, styled Shaoyou, was quite versed in letters; he was selected to marry the eleventh daughter of Emperor Taizong, Princess Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Jiao, styled Shaoyou, was quite versed in letters and was selected to marry the eleventh daughter of Emperor Taizong, Princess Anyang.

sentences.zh: 承聖二年，官至太子洗馬，秘書丞，掌東宮管記。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng he reached the posts of Groom of the Heir Apparent, Secretariat Director, and was in charge of Eastern Palace records.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chengsheng he rose to Groom of the Heir Apparent and Secretariat Director, with charge of the Eastern Palace records.

sentences.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：太清版蕩，親屬離貳，纘不能叶和籓岳，成溫陶之舉，苟懷私怨，構隙瀟湘，遂及禍於身，非由忠節；

translations.literal: Yao Cha, Minister of the Personnel Section of Chen, said: In the turmoil of Taiqing, kin turned against kin; Zuan could not harmonize the frontier princes and achieve a deed like Wen and Tao's; he harbored private resentment and opened a rift in the Xiang region, and so brought disaster upon himself — not from loyal integrity;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Cha, Minister of the Personnel Section of Chen, remarked: In the upheaval of Taiqing, kin turned against kin. Zuan could not reconcile the frontier princes as Wen and Tao had done; nursing private grievances, he opened a rift in the Xiang region and brought ruin upon himself — not out of loyal integrity;

sentences.zh: 繼以江陵淪覆，實萌於此。

translations.literal: The subsequent fall of Jiangling in truth sprouted from this.
translations.idiomatic: The subsequent fall of Jiangling had its roots in this.

sentences.zh: 以纘之風格，卒爲梁之亂階，惜矣哉。

translations.literal: By Zuan's stature and prestige, he in the end became a stair-step to Liang's disorder — how regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: Given Zuan's standing and influence, he in the end became a stepping-stone to the Liang dynasty's collapse — a tragedy indeed.
